topics.title: AWS Certified Security - Specialty
topics.summary: AWS Certified Security - Specialty is an advanced, scenario-driven certification that validates a practitioner's ability to design, implement, and operate security controls across AWS workloads, with emphasis on identity, detection, infrastructure protection, data protection, and incident response. It is aimed at security engineers, cloud security architects, and defenders who already hold an associate-level AWS certification or equivalent production experience, and who own security outcomes rat
objectives: Detection: designing and troubleshooting logging and monitoring that surfaces control-plane and data-plane events, including CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and service audit trails, and tuning findings so that real signal is not buried in noise.

Incident Response: preparing runbooks and automation for compromised credentials and workloads, containing and isolating affected resources, and preserving evidence in a form that survives later review.

Infrastructure Security: segmenting networks with VPC design, security groups, network ACLs, and edge protection, and hardening compute and container platforms against abuse and unauthorised exposure.
Identity and Access Management: building least-privilege access with IAM policies, roles, permission boundaries, and federation, and diagnosing precisely why a given request is allowed or denied.
Data Protection: selecting and operating encryption in transit and at rest, managing keys, key policies, and rotation in AWS KMS, and applying classification and lifecycle controls to stored data.
Security Foundations and Governance: applying account-level guardrails, multi-account structure, configuration baselines, and compliance reporting across an AWS organisation.
Automation and Remediation: using event-driven pipelines and infrastructure as code to correct drift and act on findings consistently instead of through manual intervention.

topics.title: AWS Certified SysOps Administrator
topics.summary: The AWS Certified SysOps Administrator - Associate exam, code SOA-C02, is aimed at engineers who already run workloads on Amazon Web Services and now want to prove they can operate them day to day. It sits at associate level, one step above the cloud practitioner entry point and alongside the solutions architect and developer associate exams, but its focus is operations rather than design or code. Passing it tells an employer that you can deploy, monitor, secure, back up and troubleshoot real ac
objectives: Explain how the AWS shared responsibility model divides security duties between the provider and the customer
Deploy and configure compute, storage and network resources using the console, the command line and templates
Collect and interpret metrics, logs and traces in order to detect and diagnose unhealthy workloads
Implement identity, access and network controls that follow least privilege and business requirements
Design backup, recovery and high availability arrangements that meet stated recovery targets
Identify and reduce unnecessary cloud spending while keeping performance acceptable

topics.title: CIS Controls Practitioner
topics.summary: The CIS Controls Practitioner (CIS-CP) certification is issued by the Center for Internet Security (CIS) for hands on security staff who put the CIS Critical Security Controls into practice. It sits at a practical, early to mid career level and suits system administrators, security analysts, engineers and consultants who must reduce risk in real networks. It proves to an employer that you can read a control, design an implementation for your environment, and measure whether it works, rather than
objectives: Describe the purpose and structure of the CIS Critical Security Controls
Choose controls that match an organisation's size, risk and resources
Build and maintain an accurate inventory of hardware, software and data
Plan secure configuration and access control for common systems
Explain how logging, monitoring and response controls work together
Measure control coverage and report progress to management

topics.title: Cisco CCNA
topics.summary: Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA) is an associate-level certification that validates the routing, switching, security and automation skills needed to install, configure, operate and troubleshoot small-to-medium enterprise networks built mainly on Cisco equipment. It is aimed at network engineers, NOC technicians, help-desk staff moving into infrastructure roles, and security practitioners who need a solid grasp of how packets actually reach their destination before they reason about what
objectives: Network fundamentals: describe the role of routers, switches, wireless access points and endpoints, and interpret the layered models that explain how traffic moves between them.
Network addressing: plan IPv4 and IPv6 schemes, subnet them to a stated requirement, and verify the result against an actual topology.
Network access: configure and verify VLANs, trunking, spanning tree behaviour, EtherChannel and basic wireless access for a small campus.
IP connectivity: bring up single-area OSPFv2, interpret the routing table, and troubleshoot a forwarding path that fails to converge.
IP services: operate NAT, DHCP, NTP, DNS clients, first-hop redundancy and quality-of-service features as they appear in a branch office.
Security fundamentals: apply device hardening, access control lists, port security, DHCP snooping and dynamic ARP inspection, and explain the threat each control addresses.

Automation and programmability: compare controller-based and traditional management, read a JSON-encoded data structure, and describe how REST APIs and configuration management tools change operations.
Troubleshooting method: use a structured, evidence-first process to isolate Layer 1 to Layer 3 faults and confirm the fix with show and debug output.

topics.title: Cisco CCNP Security
topics.summary: Cisco Certified Network Professional Security (CCNP Security) is a professional-level certification that validates the design, implementation, operation and troubleshooting of Cisco security solutions across network, cloud, content and endpoint domains. Candidates reach it through the SCOR core exam, Cisco 350-701, plus a concentration exam of their choosing, and it is intended for security engineers, architects and senior administrators who already run production controls and now need to make t
objectives: Security concepts: describe common threats, vulnerabilities, cryptographic controls and the risk-management vocabulary used to justify a security design.
Network security: deploy and troubleshoot firewall policy, intrusion prevention, segmentation and secure routing or switching controls.
Cloud security: apply identity, network, workload and data controls in public cloud environments and explain where the shared responsibility boundary sits.
Content security: configure web, email and DNS-based protections, and evaluate how inspection, decryption and policy exceptions affect their effectiveness.
Endpoint protection and detection: operate endpoint security controls, understand the telemetry they produce, and feed it into investigation workflows.
Secure network access: design remote and identity-driven access using virtual private networking, posture assessment, multi-factor authentication and zero-trust principles.
Visibility and enforcement: use network telemetry, flow data and policy enforcement points to prove what is actually happening on the estate.
Automation and integration: explain how APIs, controllers and orchestration platforms apply security policy consistently at scale.
Troubleshooting and operations: isolate faults across layered security controls and validate that a fix restores both connectivity and protection.
Architecture decisions: compare competing security designs and recommend one with an explicit statement of residual risk.

topics.title: Cisco CyberOps Associate
topics.summary: Cisco Certified CyberOps Associate is an associate-level certification that validates the daily work of a security operations centre analyst: monitoring, detecting, investigating and responding to incidents using telemetry drawn from network and endpoint sources. It suits entry-level SOC analysts, network engineers moving toward security operations, and incident responders who need a shared vocabulary for triage; it also fits experienced practitioners from adjacent domains who want structured co
objectives: Security concepts: describe the confidentiality, integrity and availability model, common threat actors, vulnerability classes, and the defensive technologies that reduce exposure.
Cryptography in operations: explain how hashing, symmetric and asymmetric encryption, certificates and TLS provide confidentiality, integrity and authentication, and where each breaks down.

Network and host telemetry: interpret data from firewalls, intrusion detection and prevention systems, proxies, flow records, endpoint agents and packet captures, and recognise what each source cannot tell you.
Security monitoring: build detection logic for common behaviours, tune it against benign activity, and reduce alert noise without dropping meaningful coverage.
Incident response process: apply preparation, identification, containment, eradication, recovery and post-incident review to a worked scenario.
Evidence handling: collect volatile and non-volatile data in a defensible order, maintain chain of custody, and document analysis so it survives later scrutiny.
Forensic analysis: examine host artefacts, memory and network evidence to reconstruct an intrusion timeline and separate attacker activity from routine administration.
Security policies and governance: relate organisational policy, compliance obligations and access control models to the analyst's daily decisions.
Vulnerability and risk context: interpret vulnerability assessment output, prioritise findings by business impact, and communicate residual risk in plain language.

topics.title: Cloud Security Alliance CCAK
topics.summary: The Certificate of Cloud Auditing Knowledge, known as CCAK, is published by the Cloud Security Alliance, or CSA, the industry body best known for its cloud controls matrix. It is aimed at auditors, risk and compliance professionals, and cloud engineers who must evidence that a cloud service is properly controlled. Unlike a purely technical cloud exam, CCAK sits at the boundary between assurance and technology: it teaches how to scope a cloud audit, how to read continuous assurance reports, and h

chapters.title: Cloud governance and enterprise risk management
Cloud assurance and auditing in practice
Cloud governance and risk management frameworks
Cloud governance, risk and compliance in the organisation

objectives: Explain cloud service and deployment models and the assurance implications of each
Apply the shared responsibility model to decide which party owns a given control
Scope a cloud audit and select the evidence needed to support a conclusion
Interpret third party assurance reports, certifications and continuous monitoring output
Assess governance, risk, compliance and identity controls in a cloud environment
Write findings and remediation advice that a cloud engineering team can act on

topics.title: Cloud Security Alliance CCSK
topics.summary: The Certificate of Cloud Security Knowledge, or CCSK, is the Cloud Security Alliance's foundational cloud security certification and the most widely recognised vendor neutral entry point into the field. It suits security analysts, architects, auditors and administrators who are moving into cloud work, and also developers and IT staff who need to understand how security changes when infrastructure is rented rather than owned. The open book, online multiple choice exam rewards understanding of the

chapters.title: Cloud governance, risk, audit and compliance
Data security, application security and security monitoring
Incident response, resilience and related technologies

objectives: Describe cloud computing concepts, architectures and service models and their security effects
Apply the shared responsibility model to divide security duties between provider and customer
Assess governance, risk, audit and compliance obligations for services you do not fully control
Explain identity, access and data protection controls used in cloud environments
Evaluate cloud infrastructure, workload, application and monitoring security
Plan incident response, resilience and recovery for cloud dependent services

topics.title: CompTIA Cloud+ (CV0-004)
topics.summary: CompTIA Cloud+ (exam code CV0-004) is a vendor neutral certification for infrastructure and operations staff who build, run and secure cloud services rather than just consume them. It sits between entry level support certifications and senior cloud architect credentials, and it assumes a few years of hands on work with servers, networks and storage. It proves that you can design a cloud solution, deploy it, secure it and keep it running when something breaks across more than one provider. The ex
objectives: Compare cloud service and deployment models and pick one that fits a stated need
Design cloud solutions for availability, scalability and cost
Apply identity, network and data security controls in a cloud environment
Deploy compute, storage and networking components to build a working solution
Run backup, monitoring and automation so services stay healthy
Troubleshoot connectivity, security, deployment and performance problems

topics.title: CompTIA CySA+ (CS0-003)
topics.summary: CompTIA CySA+ is a vendor-neutral, intermediate analyst certification that validates the ability to detect, investigate, prioritise and respond to security incidents using the data a real security operations centre produces. It is aimed at practitioners who already hold a foundational security credential or several years of hands-on experience, and who are moving into or deepening a SOC analyst, threat detection, vulnerability management or incident response role. To an employer it signals that
objectives: Security Operations: covers the collection, enrichment and correlation of security telemetry, monitoring architecture, and the workflow from alert to closure.
Vulnerability Management: covers discovery and scanning, validation of findings, false positive handling, risk-based prioritisation and remediation tracking.
Incident Response and Management: covers the response lifecycle, containment and eradication choices, evidence integrity, communication and post-incident review.
Reporting and Communication: covers vulnerability and incident reporting, metrics that inform stakeholders, and translating technical findings into business impact.
Threat Intelligence and Hunting: covers intelligence sources and sharing formats, indicator handling, threat actor profiling and hypothesis-driven hunting.
Detection Engineering and Tooling: covers rule and query logic, tuning to reduce alert fatigue, automation and orchestration, and validating detection coverage.
Network and Endpoint Analysis: covers interpreting host and network artefacts, protocol behaviour, traffic anomalies and signs of lateral movement.
Identity and Cloud Investigation: covers authentication anomaly review, cloud control plane logging, and investigating misuse of federated or service identities.

topics.title: CompTIA Linux+ (XK0-005)
topics.summary: CompTIA Linux+, exam code XK0-005, is a vendor neutral certification for administrators who already support Linux servers and want to prove it formally. It sits at a professional level, above the entry level IT certifications and alongside the server and network administrator exams, and it assumes hands on time at a command line. Passing it tells an employer that you can manage users, storage, services and permissions, harden a host, automate routine work with scripts, and diagnose faults withou
objectives: Administer users, groups, permissions and services on a Linux host
Configure storage, file systems and network settings from the command line
Harden a Linux system by applying access control, firewall and patching practices
Write shell scripts that automate repetitive administration tasks
Use containers and configuration management tools to deploy and manage workloads
Diagnose and resolve faults in storage, networking, services and application behaviour

topics.title: CompTIA Network+ (N10-009)
topics.summary: CompTIA Network+, exam code N10-009, is a vendor neutral certification for people who build and support the networks that everything else runs on. It sits at a foundation level, above basic IT support and before specialist security or cloud exams, and it suits help desk staff, junior administrators and career changers. Passing it tells an employer that you understand how data moves between systems, that you can configure and explain common network devices, and that you can diagnose a connectivit
objectives: Explain how data moves across a network using layered models and common protocols
Configure addressing, routing, switching and wireless settings for a small network
Describe cloud and virtual networking concepts and how they connect to a physical network
Apply network security controls that reduce the chance of a successful attack
Monitor, document and change a network using recognised operational practices
Troubleshoot connectivity and performance faults with a structured method and the right tools

topics.title: CompTIA PenTest+ (PT0-003)
topics.summary: CompTIA PenTest+ is a vendor-neutral, intermediate-to-advanced certification for security professionals who plan, execute and report authorised penetration testing and vulnerability assessment engagements. It suits candidates moving from defensive or administrative roles into offensive security, as well as testers who need a credential that covers the whole engagement lifecycle rather than a single exploitation toolchain. It assumes working knowledge of networking, operating systems, scripting a
objectives: Engagement Management: covers scoping, rules of engagement, legal and ethical constraints, scheduling, and managing client communication across the testing lifecycle.
Reconnaissance and Enumeration: covers passive and active information gathering, target profiling, service and application enumeration, and organising findings for later phases.
Vulnerability Discovery and Analysis: covers assessment techniques, validating suspected weaknesses, distinguishing false positives, and ranking findings by realistic impact.
Attacks and Exploitation: covers selecting and adapting techniques against authorised targets, including web, network, cloud, mobile and specialised systems.
Post-Exploitation and Lateral Movement: covers establishing and maintaining access within scope, privilege escalation awareness, discovery, and understanding data exposure risk.
Reporting and Remediation Guidance: covers documenting methodology, evidence handling, writing findings with clear impact statements, and proposing practical fixes.
Scripting and Tooling: covers adapting scripts and command-line workflows to automate enumeration, parsing and reporting tasks during an engagement.
Cloud and Container Testing: covers assessing cloud identity, storage and configuration weaknesses and understanding container and orchestration attack surface.
Communication and Professionalism: covers de-escalation, scope creep handling, safe handling of sensitive data, and presenting results to technical and non-technical audiences.

topics.title: CompTIA Security+ (SY0-701)
topics.summary: CompTIA Security+ is a vendor-neutral, entry-to-intermediate certification that validates the baseline knowledge and hands-on judgement required to work in a security operations, administration or compliance role. It is aimed at practitioners who already have some networking and systems experience and want a defensible, broadly recognised credential that covers the whole defensive surface rather than one product stack. Candidates typically come from help desk, network administration, junior SOC
objectives: General Security Concepts: covers the CIA triad, authentication and authorisation models, cryptography fundamentals, and the security implications of change management.
Threats, Vulnerabilities and Mitigations: covers threat actors and motivations, common vulnerability classes, social engineering, malware behaviour, and the controls that reduce exposure.
Security Architecture: covers secure design principles, cloud and virtualisation models, resilience and recovery, and the placement of network security controls.
Security Operations: covers monitoring and alerting, logging sources, identity and access administration, automation, and day-to-day operational hardening.
Security Program Management and Oversight: covers risk management, governance, third-party and supply chain risk, compliance obligations, auditing and security awareness.
Cryptography and PKI in Practice: covers symmetric and asymmetric primitives, hashing and keyed integrity, certificate lifecycle, and correct protocol selection.
Identity and Access Management: covers federation, multifactor authentication, privileged access handling, and the trade-offs between centralised and distributed identity.
Incident Response and Resilience: covers the response lifecycle, evidence handling basics, continuity and recovery objectives, and post-incident improvement.

topics.title: CompTIA SecurityX (CAS-005)
topics.summary: CompTIA SecurityX, exam code CAS-005, is the advanced, expert level security certification that replaced CompTIA Advanced Security Practitioner, or CASP+, in 2024. It targets senior security engineers, security architects and lead analysts who already hold a mid level certification and now design, integrate and govern security across an organisation. The exam tests judgement as much as knowledge, mixing multiple choice and performance based items in which you perform a task in a simulated enviro
objectives: Translate a business requirement into a secure architecture with defined controls and clear trade-offs
Integrate security into engineering and development workflows without blocking delivery
Analyse risk data and choose treatments that match the organisation's stated risk appetite
Design identity, access and cryptographic solutions that scale across cloud and on premises systems
Evaluate security operations, monitoring and incident response capabilities and recommend improvements
Communicate security decisions and their cost to executives, auditors and technical teams

topics.title: EC-Council CCISO
topics.summary: The Certified Chief Information Security Officer programme from EC-Council, usually shortened to CCISO, is a leadership certification rather than a technical one. It is written for people who already sit in or are moving into a senior security management role, such as a security manager, director or head of information security. The exam code is CCISO and assessment is by multiple choice examination, with the vendor also offering a separate written application requirement for the full certificat

chapters.title: Information security controls, compliance and audit management
Security programme development, operations and project management
Strategic planning, financial management and vendor management

objectives: Build a security governance structure with clear ownership, reporting lines and decision rights
Select and justify controls that reduce risk in proportion to business impact and cost
Design a security programme with measurable objectives, milestones and funding requirements
Lead and develop a security team, including skills planning and performance management
Align security strategy with business goals and present it convincingly to executives and the board

topics.title: EC-Council CEH
topics.summary: The EC-Council Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH) is a vendor-specific, knowledge-based credential that certifies a practitioner can operate like an attacker inside an authorised engagement, using the same reconnaissance, enumeration and exploitation tooling as an adversary in order to find weaknesses before someone hostile does. It suits network and system administrators, SOC analysts, auditors, developers and career changers who need a working command of offensive tradecraft rather than a single t

chapters.title: Wireless, Mobile, IoT and Operational Technology

objectives: Ethical and Legal Framework: covers authorisation, scope definition, rules of engagement, and the professional and legal limits placed on offensive testing.
Footprinting and Reconnaissance: covers passive and active information gathering against an authorised target, including open-source, DNS and infrastructure profiling.
Scanning and Enumeration: covers host discovery, port and service identification, and extracting account, share, service and directory detail from reachable systems.
Vulnerability Analysis: covers identifying and validating weaknesses, interpreting scanner output critically, and ranking issues by realistic business impact.
System Attack Techniques: covers password, privilege and access attacks against authorised hosts, including how small weaknesses are chained into a foothold.
Malware and Payload Concepts: covers how malicious software is categorised, delivered and controlled, and how defenders recognise it without handling live samples.
Sniffing, Session and Denial-of-Service Concepts: covers traffic interception, session handling weaknesses and resource-exhaustion attacks at a conceptual and defensive level.
Web, Database and Application Attacks: covers server and application weaknesses, injection classes, and the controls that reliably prevent them.
Wireless, Mobile, IoT and Operational Technology: covers the attack surface of radio, handheld, embedded and industrial environments and the controls specific to each.
Cloud and Container Attack Surface: covers identity, storage and configuration weaknesses in hosted environments and the shared-responsibility questions they raise.
Cryptography: covers encryption, hashing, PKI and common implementation mistakes, and how cryptography both protects a target and undermines it when misused.
Evasion and Defence Awareness: covers how attackers avoid detection and how firewalls, IDS and monitoring are tuned and evaded in practice.

topics.title: EC-Council CHFI
topics.summary: The EC-Council Computer Hacking Forensic Investigator (CHFI) is a vendor-specific credential that certifies a practitioner can investigate digital evidence in a forensically sound manner, from identification and seizure through acquisition, analysis and reporting, so that conclusions hold up under scrutiny in a disciplinary, regulatory or legal proceeding. It targets law enforcement and military investigators, incident responders, CSIRT and SOC staff, internal auditors, and IT professionals who

chapters.title: Evidence Handling and Chain of Custody

objectives: Forensic Readiness and Investigation Process: covers the phases of an investigation, evidence identification, documentation, and the constraints imposed by jurisdiction and organisational policy.
Evidence Handling and Chain of Custody: covers seizing, labelling, transporting and storing exhibits so that integrity and admissibility are preserved end to end.
Disk and File System Fundamentals: covers storage geometry, partitioning and file system structures, and where the metadata that supports a defensible timeline is stored.
Data Acquisition and Duplication: covers live versus dead acquisition, write blocking, imaging formats, sparse and compressed captures, and integrity verification by hashing.
Anti-Forensics and Artefact Recovery: covers recognising timestomping, hidden, slack and encrypted data, log tampering, and methods for recovering obscured evidence.
Windows Forensics: covers registry hives, event logs, prefetch, shellbags, jump lists and similar artefact families, and what each can prove about user and program activity.
Linux and macOS Forensics: covers system and authentication logs, shell history, package and service state, and platform-specific indicators of execution and persistence.
Network and Log Forensics: covers packet capture, flow records, proxy, firewall and authentication logs, and correlating network evidence with host artefacts.
Web, Email and Database Investigations: covers tracing application and mail-borne activity, header and server log analysis, and reconstructing transactions from server-side stores.
Malware and Memory Forensics: covers triaging malicious code by behaviour, volatile memory acquisition, and extracting artefacts such as injected regions and resident network state.
Mobile, Cloud and IoT Forensics: covers acquisition limits on handheld and embedded devices, evidence held by hosted services, and the shared-responsibility questions that follow.
Reporting and Expert Testimony: covers writing defensible findings, presenting timelines and opinion clearly, and withstanding cross-examination on method and interpretation.

topics.title: EC-Council CND
topics.summary: The Certified Network Defender (CND) from EC-Council is a defensive certification for network and security operations staff who protect an enterprise network rather than attack it. It sits at a mid level, above first line support and below advanced incident response or forensics credentials, and it suits network administrators moving into security operations, junior analysts and system administrators with security duties. It proves to an employer that you can read network traffic, harden devices

chapters.title: Network security controls, protocols and devices
Network security policy design and implementation
Network security monitoring and incident response

objectives: Explain how data moves through a network and where it can be attacked
Identify common network attacks and the weaknesses they exploit
Configure firewalls, intrusion detection and prevention systems, and virtual private networks
Write and apply network security policy, hardening baselines and access control
Monitor network traffic and detect suspicious activity
Respond to a network incident, contain it and support recovery

topics.title: EC-Council CPENT
topics.summary: The Certified Penetration Testing Professional (CPENT) from EC-Council is an advanced, hands on penetration testing certification for testers who already work in the field and want to prove it under pressure. It sits well above entry level offensive credentials and expects prior experience with enumeration, exploitation and privilege escalation on both Linux and Windows. The exam is entirely practical. You attack live target networks in a controlled lab over two sessions, usually a shorter first

chapters.title: Scoping, engagement planning and professional conduct
Reconnaissance and enumeration of systems and services
Exploitation of Linux and Windows systems
Web application and client side exploitation
Specialised systems including IoT, OT and cloud
Post exploitation, reporting and remediation advice

objectives: Plan and scope a penetration test within legal and contractual limits
Gather intelligence on targets and enumerate services on Linux and Windows systems
Exploit identified weaknesses to gain a foothold on target hosts
Escalate privileges and move through segmented networks using pivoting
Test web applications, binaries and specialised systems for exploitable flaws
Write a professional report that explains risk and gives clear remediation advice

topics.title: EC-Council CSA
topics.summary: The Certified SOC Analyst (CSA) from EC-Council is an entry to intermediate certification for people who work, or want to work, on the front line of a security operations centre. A security operations centre is the team that watches alerts and responds to them around the clock. It sits above general information technology certifications and below advanced incident response or forensics credentials, and it suits help desk and network staff moving into security, plus new analysts who need a struct
objectives: Explain how a security operations centre is organised and how analysts work in shifts
Triage alerts and decide which ones need investigation and which are noise
Collect and interpret logs and evidence from common security tools
Follow an incident handling process from detection through containment and closure
Use threat intelligence to add context to a security event
Support vulnerability assessment and reporting duties for the security team

topics.title: EC-Council ECIH
topics.summary: The EC-Council Certified Incident Handler (ECIH, exam code ECIH) is an intermediate-level certification for security analysts who deal with live incidents. It suits SOC analysts, help desk engineers moving into security operations, and administrators who must contain a breach before it spreads. It proves to an employer that you can follow a recognised incident handling process, from preparation through containment, eradication and recovery to lessons learned. The exam is a knowledge test of mult

chapters.title: Introduction to Incident Handling and Response
Attacker Frameworks and the Incident Handling Lifecycle
Handling Web Application and Server Incidents

objectives: Explain the difference between a security event, an incident and a breach using the words correctly.
Describe the incident handling lifecycle and the activities performed at each stage.
Identify the common attack categories that cause incidents and the evidence each one leaves behind.
Outline the first response steps for a malware, email, web or network incident.
Describe how to preserve evidence so that later investigation stays trustworthy.
Produce a short incident report that states impact, actions taken and lessons learned.

topics.title: Elastic Certified Analyst
topics.summary: The Elastic Certified Analyst (exam code ECA) is a hands-on certification for people who investigate data in the Elastic Stack, which is a search and analytics platform built around Elasticsearch for storage and Kibana for exploration. It suits SOC analysts, observability engineers and administrators who already work with logs and want proof they can answer real questions with the platform. It proves to an employer that you can bring data in, shape it, search it, build a view of it and reach a d
objectives: Explain how documents, fields and mappings decide what a search can and cannot find.
Bring log data into the platform from a source and confirm that the events arrived correctly.
Write queries that filter, group and summarise data to answer a specific question.
Build charts and a dashboard that let another person see the same answer quickly.
Investigate a security alert by following evidence across several event types.
Describe your findings from a dataset accurately and state the limits of what the data proves.

topics.title: Fortinet NSE 4
topics.summary: Fortinet NSE 4 (exam code NSE4) is an associate level certification for engineers who deploy and run FortiGate firewalls, which are network devices that control traffic between networks. It suits network engineers, security administrators and support staff who already handle routing and switching basics. It proves to an employer that you can set up a firewall from a blank device, write policies that allow only the traffic a business needs, apply inspection profiles to that traffic, and build enc
objectives: Explain the role of a firewall in a network and how it fits between the internet and internal systems.
Initialise a firewall device, register it, and complete the basic setup needed before it protects anything.
Write security policies that permit or deny traffic according to a stated business requirement.
Apply inspection profiles such as antivirus and web filtering to the traffic that passes a policy.
Configure encrypted tunnels that connect two sites or allow staff to work from home safely.
Diagnose a traffic problem using logs and command line tools, and describe the likely cause.

topics.title: GIAC GCED
topics.summary: The GIAC Certified Enterprise Defender (GCED) is an advanced certification for defenders who must understand both how networks are attacked and how to stop those attacks. It suits experienced SOC analysts, incident responders, network security engineers and defenders preparing for a broad role rather than a single specialism. It proves to an employer that you can explain protocol weaknesses, choose detective and preventive controls, read packet captures, triage malware, and take part in a penetr

chapters.title: Malware Analysis Concepts, Basic and Interactive Techniques
Network Security Monitoring Concepts and Application
Network Forensics, Logging and Event Management

objectives: Explain how common network protocols work and how each one can be abused by an attacker.
Choose detective and preventive controls that fit a specific risk in a network or cloud environment.
Read a packet capture and describe what happened between two hosts.
Triage a suspicious file safely and describe what it does and what it leaves behind.
Follow a continuous incident response process from detection through to lessons learned.
Explain the scope, rules and reporting stages of a penetration test from the defender's point of view.

topics.title: GIAC GCFA
topics.summary: The GIAC Certified Forensic Analyst (GCFA) is an advanced, hands on certification for analysts who investigate compromised computers and prove what happened on them. It suits incident responders, threat hunters, forensic examiners and experienced SOC analysts who already read host data as part of their job. It proves to an employer that you can collect volatile evidence, analyse memory, rebuild a file system timeline, spot anti forensic tricks, and write findings that would survive scrutiny in a

chapters.title: Introduction to File System Timeline Forensics
Identification of Normal System and User Activity
Identification of Malicious System and User Activity

objectives: Explain the difference between volatile and non volatile evidence and why the order of collection matters.
Collect memory and disk evidence in a way that keeps it trustworthy and repeatable.
Analyse memory to identify running processes, network connections and injected code.
Interpret Windows artefacts such as registry keys, prefetch records and event logs.
Build a timeline from several artefact sources and explain the sequence of activity it shows.
Recognise anti forensic techniques and describe how to detect them anyway.

topics.title: GIAC GCIA
topics.summary: GIAC GCIA (Global Information Assurance Certification Certified Intrusion Analyst) is an advanced, vendor-neutral certification for analysts who detect and characterise intrusions from network and host telemetry. It is aimed at senior security operations analysts, network security engineers, threat hunters and forensic practitioners who already read packets and logs fluently and want to prove they can reconstruct activity from raw evidence rather than from a vendor console summary. Passing the e
objectives: Network traffic analysis fundamentals: Read packet captures at the protocol level and distinguish normal behaviour from anomalies in the protocols most commonly abused.
TCP and IP behaviour: Explain connection state, fragmentation, tunnelling and encapsulation well enough to recognise traffic that has been deliberately manipulated.
Application layer protocols: Interpret domain name resolution, web, mail, file transfer and remote access exchanges, and identify how each is used for legitimate or hostile purposes.
Intrusion detection and signature engineering: Interpret, write and tune detection signatures while accounting for false positives, evasion techniques and performance limits.
Traffic baselining and anomaly detection: Establish what normal looks like for a given network, then reason about deviations without over-trusting statistical outliers.
Flow and metadata analysis: Use flow records and similar metadata to scope activity, identify regular beaconing and reconstruct connections at a scale packet capture cannot reach.
Host and log correlation: Combine system, application and security logs with network evidence to confirm an intrusion rather than infer one from a single source.
Attack patterns in evidence: Recognise reconnaissance, tunnelling, command and control, and exfiltration patterns from the artefacts each leaves behind.
Analyst reporting and escalation: Document findings, confidence levels and next investigative steps so that a peer can reproduce the conclusion.

topics.title: GIAC GCIH
topics.summary: GIAC GCIH (Global Information Assurance Certification Certified Incident Handler) is an advanced, vendor-neutral certification centred on detecting, containing, eradicating and recovering from security incidents, including the adversary techniques that create them. It targets experienced security operations analysts, incident responders, forensic examiners and consultants who already understand host and network fundamentals and now need to run an investigation from first alert to final report un
objectives: Incident response lifecycle: Apply preparation, identification, containment, eradication, recovery and post-incident review to a live intrusion, and justify each decision against the phase it belongs to.
Adversary techniques and tradecraft: Interpret common initial access, execution, persistence, privilege escalation and lateral movement behaviour from the defender's position.
Detection and triage: Build hunt hypotheses, prioritise alerts and separate true positives from environmental noise using host, network and identity telemetry.
Volatile evidence handling: Order the collection of memory, process, network and session state so perishable evidence survives before any shutdown or remediation step.
Host and memory investigation: Interpret process trees, autostart locations, services, scheduled execution and memory artefacts to identify malicious execution and persistence.
Network evidence and containment: Use flow and packet evidence to scope an intrusion, then contain it without alerting the adversary or corrupting the record of what happened.
Malware and tooling triage: Characterise suspicious binaries and scripts safely, describe observed behaviour, and decide what to block, isolate or hunt for next.
Eradication and recovery: Verify removal of adversary access, restore services in a controlled order, and define the monitoring that confirms the environment stays clean.
Communication and reporting: Produce timelines, findings, confidence statements and recommendations that serve both technical peers and executive decision makers.

topics.title: GIAC GISP
topics.summary: The GIAC Information Security Professional, exam code GISP, is a broad foundation certification from the Global Information Assurance Certification body. GIAC is the certification arm of the SANS Institute, a well known security training organisation. This exam suits security analysts, administrators and managers who need wide coverage of security principles rather than deep work in one tool. Passing it shows an employer that you understand access control, cryptography, business continuity, law
objectives: Describe how access control models protect systems and data.
Explain how cryptography is applied to protect stored and moving information.
Plan for business continuity and disaster recovery in an organisation.
Identify the laws, standards and duties that affect security work.
Outline how networks and telecommunications are secured in practice.
Apply operations security controls to everyday administration tasks.

topics.title: GIAC GMON
topics.summary: The GIAC Continuous Monitoring Certification, exam code GMON, is a defensive security certification from GIAC, the certification body of the SANS Institute. It is built for security operations centre analysts, incident responders and threat hunters who already work with logs and alerts. Passing it shows an employer that you can design detection, collect the right telemetry, spot suspicious activity in Linux and Windows hosts and in network traffic, and follow an incident through to a conclusion.

chapters.title: Continuous monitoring and security operations foundations
Linux host and application attack detection
Windows host and application attack detection

objectives: Explain the phases of continuous monitoring and how detection fits into security operations.
Identify the log and telemetry sources that reveal attacker activity.
Recognise common attack patterns on Linux and Windows hosts.
Build detection content and tune it to reduce false alarms.
Investigate an alert and document the findings clearly.
Support incident response with evidence collected from monitoring data.

topics.title: GIAC GPEN
topics.summary: The GIAC Penetration Tester certification, exam code GPEN, is an offensive security credential from GIAC, the certification body of the SANS Institute. It suits penetration testers, red team operators and security consultants who already run authorised assessments against networks and hosts. Passing it shows an employer that you can scope an engagement, perform reconnaissance, exploit weaknesses in network services and operating systems, raise your privileges and move carefully through a target

chapters.title: Network essentials and defence in depth
Planning and scoping a penetration test
Exploitation of network services and systems
Privilege escalation, lateral movement and reporting

objectives: Explain the legal and ethical rules that govern an authorised penetration test.
Plan an engagement and define its scope, targets and limits.
Gather information about a target using passive and active techniques.
Exploit known weaknesses in network services and operating systems.
Escalate privileges and move between hosts after an initial foothold.
Report findings with clear evidence and practical fixes.

topics.title: GIAC GSEC
topics.summary: GIAC GSEC (Global Information Assurance Certification Security Essentials) is an entry-level, vendor-neutral certification that validates broad, practical knowledge of information security across networks, endpoints, cloud workloads and the policies that hold them together. It is aimed at practitioners early in a security career: SOC analysts, system and network administrators moving into a security role, and consultants who must demonstrate a working command of defensive fundamentals rather tha
objectives: Access controls and password management: Explain how authentication factors, credential storage, account lifecycle and privilege assignment interact, and how weak configurations are abused in practice.

Cryptography and public key infrastructure: Describe symmetric and asymmetric primitives, hashing and message authentication, certificate issuance and validation, and the trust assumptions that break under interception.
Defensible network architecture: Apply segmentation, demilitarised zone design, boundary filtering and monitoring placement, and reason about where zero-trust assumptions change the design.
Windows and Linux host security: Interpret hardening baselines, service and permission configuration, logging sources and endpoint protection behaviour across both operating system families.

Network security technologies: Compare firewall, intrusion detection and prevention, proxy, virtual private network and network access control behaviour, including the traffic each technology cannot see.
Wireless and remote access security: Evaluate authentication and encryption choices for wireless and remote access, and identify misconfigurations that expose credentials or traffic.
Virtualisation, cloud and DevOps security: Map shared responsibility, identity and key management, image and pipeline controls, and the configuration drift that appears after deployment.
Incident response and contingency planning: Describe preparation, identification, containment, eradication, recovery and lessons learned, and the evidence each phase depends on.
Risk, policy and compliance: Translate control frameworks, policy language, business impact analysis and audit expectations into defensible operational decisions.

topics.title: GIAC GWAPT
topics.summary: The GIAC Web Application Penetration Tester certification, exam code GWAPT, is a specialist offensive security credential from GIAC, the certification body of the SANS Institute. It is aimed at penetration testers, application security engineers and developers who need to assess web applications rather than whole networks. Passing it shows an employer that you understand how a modern web application is built and how it can be attacked, including reconnaissance, authentication and session flaws,

chapters.title: Reconnaissance and mapping of a web application
Application logic, other flaws and reporting

objectives: Describe how browsers, servers and web technologies exchange data.
Map the visible surface of a web application before testing it.
Test authentication, authorisation and session handling for weaknesses.
Find and confirm injection flaws without damaging the target.
Assess client side attacks that affect a user browser session.
Explain application logic flaws and recommend practical fixes.

topics.title: GIAC GXPN
topics.summary: The GIAC Exploit Researcher and Advanced Penetration Tester certification, exam code GXPN, is an advanced offensive security credential from GIAC, the certification body of the SANS Institute. It suits experienced penetration testers, exploit developers, red team operators and security researchers who already understand basic testing and now want to attack hardened systems. Passing it shows an employer that you can research a target, defeat modern memory protections, write and adapt working proo
objectives: Explain how memory is organised and how modern protections change an attack.
Analyse network protocols and services for exploitable behaviour.
Identify and exploit weaknesses in cryptographic implementations and keys.
Develop and adapt working proof of concept code against a target.
Bypass host protections and escalate privileges on a hardened system.
Use reverse engineering and fuzzing to find new software flaws.

topics.title: Google Associate Cloud Engineer
topics.summary: The Google Associate Cloud Engineer credential, exam code ACE, is an entry to mid level certification from Google Cloud for people who deploy and operate workloads on that platform. It suits system administrators, cloud engineers and support staff with roughly six months of hands on Google Cloud experience. Passing it shows an employer that you can set up a cloud project, deploy an application, monitor its health and manage identity, networking and cost controls with the console and the command

Ensuring successful operation of a cloud solution

Deploy applications using virtual machines, containers and managed platforms.
Implement storage options and decide when object storage is the right choice.
Use monitoring, logging and alerting to keep an environment healthy.

objectives: Configuring access: designing Cloud Identity and IAM policy at organization, folder, project and resource level, including service accounts, workload identity federation, groups and least-privilege role selection.

Securing workloads and containers: hardening GKE and serverless deployments, image provenance and binary authorization, runtime isolation and supply chain controls.
Automating security operations: expressing guardrails as infrastructure as code, policy as code, continuous posture assessment and repeatable remediation pipelines.
Responding to incidents: investigating with logs and asset inventory, containing compromised identities and workloads, and validating recovery of affected services.

topics.title: IAPP CIPP/E

topics.title: INE eJPT

It suits students, help desk staff, system administrators and developers who understand basic networking and want proof of practical skill. topics.title: ISACA CDPSE
topics.summary: The Certified Data Privacy Solutions Engineer (CDPSE) is an ISACA certification for experienced privacy and technology professionals who build privacy into systems rather than only writing policy. objectives: Describe how privacy governance fits with an organisation's overall risk and compliance work

Identify where personal data is collected, moved, stored and shared across a business

topics.title: ISACA CGEIT
topics.summary: Certified in the Governance of Enterprise IT (CGEIT) is an ISACA certification for experienced professionals who direct, manage and assure information technology (IT) from a governance point of view. objectives: Explain how an enterprise governance of IT framework is set up in a real organisation

topics.title: ISACA CISA
topics.summary: The Certified Information Systems Auditor is ISACA's established credential for professionals who audit, assure and control information systems, and it remains the reference qualification for IT audit roles in banking, government, healthcare and large enterprise internal audit functions. It suits external and internal auditors, control and compliance analysts, security and risk practitioners who support audits, and technology managers responsible for the control environment. objectives: Information Systems Auditing Process: Plan, scope and conduct audits by applying risk-based approaches, IS audit standards and guidelines, and professional ethics and independence requirements.

Information Systems Operations and Business Resilience: Evaluate backup, restoration testing, disaster recovery and business continuity arrangements against recovery objectives and dependencies, including for outsourced services.

Protection of Information Assets: Assess security programme management, incident response and monitoring, awareness and training, data classification and privacy obligations, and the adequacy of security testing.

topics.title: ISACA CISM
topics.summary: The Certified Information Security Manager is ISACA's advanced credential for professionals who build, run and govern an enterprise information security programme rather than operate individual controls. To an employer the certification signals that the holder can align security investment w
objectives: Information Security Governance: Establish and maintain a security governance framework that aligns security strategy, objectives and metrics with enterprise goals, and define roles, reporting lines and oversight responsibilities.
Information Security Governance: Develop, approve and communicate policy, standards and procedures, and evaluate whether the governance structure actually produces accountable, measurable decisions.

Information Security Risk Management: Identify, assess and prioritise information risk using qualitative and quantitative methods, define risk appetite and tolerance, and maintain a risk register with owners.
Information Security Risk Management: Select and justify risk treatment options and control objectives, monitor residual risk, and communicate risk exposure to stakeholders in business terms.

Information Security Programme Development: Build and maintain a security programme, including architecture, control selection, awareness and training, and the metrics used to demonstrate programme effectiveness.

Information Security Programme Development: Assess current capability maturity, plan programme improvements and resource them, and integrate security requirements into business processes and third-party relationships.
Information Security Incident Management: Develop and maintain an incident response plan covering preparation, detection, containment, eradication, recovery and post-incident review.

Information Security Incident Management: Classify incidents by business impact, coordinate response across technical and business teams, and handle evidence, notification and regulatory reporting obligations.
Business Continuity and Resilience: Align incident and continuity planning so that recovery objectives, dependencies and communications are consistent across security and resilience functions.
Metrics and Reporting: Define and report security and risk metrics that support executive decisions rather than vanity statistics, and use them to steer programme priorities.

topics.title: ISACA CRISC
topics.summary: The Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control credential is ISACA's qualification for practitioners who own technology risk and the control environment that answers it, spanning both IT risk identification and the design, monitoring and maintenance of controls. It is aimed at risk managers, control and compliance leads, security and audit professionals who want to move from operating controls to governing risk, and business-facing technologists responsible for a risk register or regulato
objectives: IT Risk Governance: Establish and maintain a risk governance framework that defines risk appetite, tolerance, roles, accountability and escalation paths across the enterprise.
IT Risk Governance: Align IT risk management with enterprise risk management, legal and regulatory obligations, and business strategy, and communicate the aggregated risk profile to oversight bodies.

IT Risk Assessment: Identify IT risk events and contributing factors across processes, projects, assets and third parties, using techniques such as threat and vulnerability analysis and scenario analysis.

IT Risk Assessment: Analyse and evaluate inherent and residual risk using qualitative and quantitative methods, prioritise exposures, and document the analysis so that it can be reviewed and relied upon.

Risk Response and Reporting: Select and justify risk response options including avoidance, mitigation, transfer and acceptance, and ensure remediation, ownership and deadlines are agreed with accountable parties.
Risk Response and Reporting: Monitor and report risk and control status with meaningful metrics and key risk indicators, and validate that reported improvements are supported by reliable evidence.
Information Technology and Security: Design and implement controls that address identified risk across identity and access, change, operations, data protection and third-party arrangements.
Information Technology and Security: Assess whether controls are designed effectively and operating as intended, and maintain them as business, threat and technology conditions change.

Information Technology and Security: Evaluate the risk implications of emerging technology, architecture change and outsourcing decisions before commitment, and integrate risk considerations into project and change lifecycles.
Control Ownership and Culture: Embed risk awareness and control accountability into business and technology teams so that risk decisions are made and recorded at the right level.

topics.title: ISC2 CCSP
topics.summary: The Certified Cloud Security Professional (CCSP) is an ISC2 credential that validates the ability to secure cloud-hosted systems and data across the full cloud life cycle, from architecture and design through operation, audit, and contractual governance. It is aimed at experienced security practitioners, cloud architects, and risk and compliance staff who already understand general security fundamentals and now need depth specific to shared responsibility, multi-tenant infrastructure, and the wa
objectives: Cloud Concepts, Architecture and Design: cloud reference architecture, service and deployment models, the shared responsibility model, cloud security design principles, and evaluating cloud migration and provider capability.

Cloud Data Security: data classification and discovery in cloud environments, cloud data life cycle stages, storage architecture and technologies, data protection mechanisms including encryption and key custody, and data retention, deletion and archiving.

Cloud Platform and Infrastructure Security: physical and logical infrastructure for cloud, workload and network security design, management plane protection, business continuity and disaster recovery planning in cloud, and assessing and remediating platform risk.

Cloud Application Security: secure software development life cycle in cloud, training and awareness for cloud development, identity and access management integration for applications, application architecture and API security, and validating cloud application security before and after deployment.

Cloud Security Operations: operating and maintaining cloud infrastructure, change and configuration management, monitoring logging and alerting, incident response in cloud, and supporting digital forensics with cloud-resident evidence.

Legal, Risk and Compliance: legal requirements and unique cloud risks, privacy considerations and jurisdictional issues, audit processes and assurance reporting, cloud contract and vendor management, and the impact of emerging technologies on cloud governance.

topics.title: ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC)
topics.summary: Certified in Cybersecurity (CC) is ISC2's entry-level credential, designed to demonstrate that a candidate understands the foundational principles and operational vocabulary of information security before specialising. It is aimed at career changers, graduates, IT support and helpdesk staff, and anyone taking a first step toward a security role, and it assumes no prior professional security experience. For an employer, CC signals baseline literacy: the holder can explain confidentiality, integri

chapters.title: Business Continuity, Disaster Recovery and Incident Response Concepts

objectives: Security Principles: confidentiality, integrity and availability, authentication factors and authorisation concepts, privacy, risk management fundamentals, and the relationship between vulnerabilities, threats and risk.

Information Security Governance and Controls: security policies, procedures and standards, administrative, technical and physical control categories, control functions such as preventive, detective and corrective, and professional ethics and legal awareness.

Business Continuity, Disaster Recovery and Incident Response Concepts: business impact considerations, recovery objectives and continuity strategies, the phases of incident response, and the roles and communication paths used when an event escalates.

Access Control Concepts: identification, authentication and authorisation in practice, physical and logical access controls, least privilege and separation of duties, and the provisioning and deprovisioning life cycle.

Network Security: network architecture and device roles, common network attacks and countermeasures, secure communication and remote access methods, and protecting wireless and cloud-connected environments.

Security Operations: security operations centre functions, logging and monitoring, vulnerability and patch management, change management, and the day-to-day activities that keep controls effective and evidence available.

topics.title: ISC2 CISSP
topics.summary: The Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) is a vendor-neutral, senior-level credential that validates the ability to design, engineer, and govern an organisation's security programme across eight domains of practice rather than a single technology stack. It is aimed at practitioners with several years of hands-on security responsibility who are moving from operating controls to owning risk decisions: security architects, SOC and IR leads, consultants, auditors, and managers
objectives: Security and Risk Management: confidentiality, integrity and availability, security governance principles, compliance and legal obligations, policy and procedure development, business continuity planning, and personnel security.

Asset Security: information and asset classification, ownership and handling requirements, privacy protection, data retention and secure destruction, and establishing handling standards across the asset life cycle.

Security Architecture and Engineering: secure design principles, security models, cryptography and key management, physical security, and site and facility design considerations for resisting and detecting compromise.

Communication and Network Security: secure network architecture and design, network component hardening, secure communication channels, and mitigating attacks against network availability and integrity.

Identity and Access Management: identification and authentication, authorisation mechanisms and access control models, federation and third-party identity services, and the identity life cycle including provisioning and deprovisioning.

Security Assessment and Testing: assessment and testing strategies, vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, security control testing, audit logging, and interpreting test results for decision makers.
Security Operations: investigations and evidence handling, logging and monitoring, incident management, disaster recovery, change and configuration management, and resource protection and continuity.

Software Development Security: integrating security into the development life cycle, secure coding and development environment controls, acquired software and supply-chain risk, and assessing software security effectiveness.

topics.title: ISC2 CISSP-ISSAP

Prepare a system and its data for safe disposal or transfer

topics.title: ISC2 CISSP-ISSMP
topics.summary: The Information Systems Security Management Professional (ISSMP) is an advanced concentration exam from ISC2 for people who already hold the Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) and want to be judged on management rather than hands on engineering. objectives: Build a security programme that matches the organisation's strategy and risk appetite
Lead and organise a security team, including hiring, training and measuring performance
