topics.title: ISO/IEC 27005 Lead Risk Manager
topics.summary: The ISO/IEC 27005 Lead Risk Manager is a professional certification for people who run information security risk management rather than merely take part in it. It is built on the guidance in ISO/IEC 27005 and is delivered by accredited training bodies, so the standard is exam code 27005 rather than a vendor exam number. The level sits between practitioner and manager: candidates are expected to know the vocabulary of risk, to apply a repeatable method, and to explain their decisions to auditors

chapters.title: Concepts and definitions of information security risk
Establishing context, scope and risk criteria
Risk management methods and continual improvement

objectives: Explain the concepts, terms and principles that information security risk management uses
Establish context and scope so that risk decisions match the organisation and its obligations
Identify, analyse and evaluate risk with a method that another person could repeat
Select and document risk treatment options, including the acceptance of residual risk
Describe how risk is communicated to owners, executives and other interested parties
Monitor, review and improve a risk management process over time

topics.title: Linux Foundation CKS
topics.summary: The Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist (CKS) is an advanced, performance-based certification that proves a candidate can secure containerised workloads and the Kubernetes clusters that run them. It is intended for engineers who already administer Kubernetes competently and now carry responsibility for its security posture: platform engineers, DevSecOps practitioners, cloud security architects and incident responders who operate clusters in regulated or internet-facing environments. Unlike
objectives: Cluster Setup: harden cluster components, restrict network access to the control plane, apply CIS-style benchmark checks and verify the resulting configuration.
Cluster Hardening: manage role-based access control tightly, limit service account permissions, and understand how API server flags and admission controls interact.
System Hardening: minimise the host attack surface, constrain IAM and node access, and reason about the trade-off between usability and least privilege.
Minimise Microservice Vulnerabilities: apply security contexts, pod security admission, sealed secrets and runtime sandboxing to reduce container breakout risk.
Supply Chain Security: verify image provenance and integrity, sign and scan artefacts, and enforce policy over what may be deployed into the cluster.
Monitoring, Logging and Runtime Security: enable audit logging, detect behavioural anomalies in workloads, and investigate compromised containers with immutable evidence.
Network Security: write and test network policies, secure ingress paths, and reason about segmentation between namespaces and tenants.
Secrets and Configuration Management: store and rotate sensitive material safely, and avoid exposing credentials through environment variables or mounted files.
Incident Response in Kubernetes: isolate a suspect workload, preserve forensic artefacts, and recover a cluster without destroying evidence.

topics.title: Linux Foundation KCNA
topics.summary: The Kubernetes and Cloud Native Associate, exam code KCNA, is an entry level certification from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, which is hosted by the Linux Foundation. It is aimed at people who are starting to work with containers and Kubernetes and who want a formal, vendor neutral first step before a deeper administrator exam. The level is associate, so the paper tests broad understanding of the ecosystem rather than deep cluster surgery. Passing it tells an employer that you know how
objectives: Explain what Kubernetes is and how it differs from running containers by hand
Describe the main Kubernetes objects and the job each one performs
Explain container orchestration concerns such as scheduling, scaling and self healing
Describe how cloud native applications are packaged, delivered and released
Explain observability, including logs, metrics and traces, and why it matters in production
Identify the wider cloud native ecosystem, including the projects around Kubernetes

topics.title: Linux Foundation LFCS
topics.summary: The Linux Foundation Certified System Administrator (LFCS) is a performance-based certification that validates a candidate's ability to operate, configure and troubleshoot a live Linux system rather than recall facts about one. It is aimed at working system administrators, DevOps engineers, site reliability engineers and security practitioners who already touch Linux hosts daily and need an externally recognised proof of operational competence, not at beginners looking for a first introduction t
objectives: Essential Commands: navigate the filesystem, manipulate files and text streams, use package management, and work efficiently with shell pipelines and redirection.
Operations Deployment: manage the boot process, kernel parameters and systemd units, schedule recurring work, and keep services running across reboots.
User and Group Management: create and modify accounts and groups, configure sudo delegation, and reason about password ageing and login policy.
Networking: configure interfaces, addresses, routes, hostname resolution and firewall rules, and diagnose connectivity problems from the host itself.
Storage Management: partition and format disks, manage LVM volumes, create and mount filesystems including network filesystems, and persist mounts via fstab.
Service Configuration: deploy and tune common server roles such as web, database, DNS, file sharing and time synchronisation, and validate them locally.
Security and Access Control: apply file permissions, ACLs and special bits, configure SELinux or AppArmor modes, and manage SSH access and key material.
Scripting and Automation: write shell scripts that accept arguments, test conditions, loop safely and exit with meaningful status codes for automation to consume.
Troubleshooting: read system and service logs, isolate failures in boot, networking, storage and permissions, and restore a working state without a reboot where possible.

topics.title: Microsoft AZ-500 Azure Security Engineer
topics.summary: Microsoft AZ-500 Azure Security Engineer Associate is an intermediate-level certification that validates the ability to implement and operate security controls across Azure identities, networks, compute, data and platform monitoring. Candidates are cloud engineers, security engineers and administrators who already deploy and manage Azure resources and are now accountable for hardening, detecting and evidencing the security of those workloads. For an employer the credential indicates that the hol
objectives: Identity and access management: Configure Microsoft Entra ID tenants, users and groups, authentication methods including multifactor and passwordless, conditional access, and identity protection signals.

Privileged and workload identity: Implement privileged identity management, managed identities, service principals and app registration permissions following least privilege for human and machine identities.
Network security: Design and configure network security groups, Azure Firewall, DDoS protection, private endpoints and secure hybrid connectivity, including effective rule evaluation order.
Compute security: Harden virtual machines, containers, Azure Kubernetes Service and serverless workloads with endpoint protection, patching, just-in-time access and secure baseline configuration.

Storage and database security: Apply encryption, customer-managed keys via Key Vault, network restrictions, authentication options and data classification controls across storage accounts, Azure SQL and Cosmos DB.
Cloud security posture: Configure Microsoft Defender for Cloud plans, security policies and regulatory compliance views, then prioritise and remediate posture recommendations by risk.
Detection and response: Deploy Microsoft Sentinel for Azure telemetry, write KQL queries across identity, network and compute logs, and respond to alerts with documented containment steps.
Governance and policy at scale: Use Azure Policy, role-based access control, resource locks and tagging to enforce and audit security baselines across subscriptions and management groups.

topics.title: Microsoft SC-100 Cybersecurity Architect
topics.summary: Microsoft SC-100 Cybersecurity Architect is an expert-level certification for professionals who design and evolve security strategy rather than operate individual controls. Candidates are typically senior security engineers, solution architects, consultants or security leads who must translate business risk and regulatory obligation into an architecture spanning on-premises, Azure, multicloud and hybrid estates. Microsoft requires an active qualifying prerequisite certification before the exam c
objectives: Zero Trust strategy and architecture: Translate business requirements into a Zero Trust blueprint, define posture targets, and select identity-first controls across hybrid, Azure and multicloud estates.
Resilience and recovery design: Design segmentation, backup, immutability and recovery sequencing that keeps ransomware from becoming an existential event.
Identity and access design: Specify identity governance, privileged access, conditional access, passwordless authentication and workload identity patterns for human and non-human identities.
Security operations strategy: Define SOC structure, SIEM and SOAR architecture, threat intelligence integration, and the metrics such as mean time to detect and respond that steer the programme.

Governance, risk and compliance: Map regulatory and contractual obligations to technical controls, design for data residency and sovereignty, and align to frameworks such as ISO 27001 and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
Infrastructure security: Design protection for servers, endpoints, OT and IoT, containers, Kubernetes and hybrid workloads, including patching and configuration baselines at scale.
Data and application security: Specify classification, encryption and key management, secrets handling, and secure development lifecycle controls for applications, APIs and data stores.
Evaluation and recommendation: Compare competing technical options, produce architecture recommendations for executive stakeholders, and justify cost, risk and operational trade-offs.
Emerging and third-party risk: Incorporate cloud-native services, AI-enabled workloads and supply chain dependencies into architecture decisions and assurance activities.

topics.title: Microsoft SC-200 Security Operations Analyst
topics.summary: Microsoft SC-200 Security Operations Analyst is an associate-level certification that validates the ability to detect, investigate and respond to threats using Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel. It is aimed at security analysts who already work in a security operations centre or are moving into one, and it assumes working familiarity with Windows and Linux fundamentals, networking, and at least some Microsoft 365 and Azure administration. For an employer
objectives: Defender XDR fundamentals: Explain how signals from Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Office 365, Defender for Identity and Defender for Cloud Apps are correlated into a unified alert and incident model.
Threat investigation in Defender XDR: Use advanced hunting queries, alert triage views, entity and evidence panes, and automated investigation to establish scope, root cause and blast radius.
Incident response actions: Apply containment and remediation actions such as device isolation, live response, mailbox remediation and app governance, and record the reasoning behind each decision.

Microsoft Defender for Cloud: Assess cloud security posture, interpret secure score recommendations, and prioritise misconfigurations and workload protection gaps across Azure and multicloud resources.

Sentinel data ingestion: Connect data sources with built-in connectors, codeless connectors and the Logs Ingestion API, then validate parsing and normalisation into the advanced security information model.
Detection engineering: Author scheduled, near-real-time and fusion analytics rules in KQL, tune rule thresholds against false positives, and manage detection content in a version-controlled workflow.
Hunting and automation: Build hunting queries and workbooks for proactive threat hunting, and implement Logic Apps playbooks that automate triage and response steps consistently.
Incident management in Microsoft Sentinel: Triage, assign, collaborate on and close incidents, including entity mapping, task tracking and defensible evidence handling.

topics.title: Microsoft SC-300 Identity and Access Administrator
topics.shortTitle: Microsoft SC-300 Identity and Access Administrator
topics.summary: Exam SC-300 is Microsoft's associate level certification for identity and access administrators, and passing it earns the Microsoft Certified: Identity and Access Administrator Associate title. It suits engineers who already work with Microsoft Entra ID, the cloud directory formerly named Azure Active Directory, and who now need to design, run and troubleshoot sign in, access and governance for a whole tenant. The exam mixes multiple choice questions with scenario based items, so it tests decisi
objectives: Explain what the SC-300 certification proves and which roles it supports
Describe how Microsoft Entra ID stores and manages identities
Choose the right authentication control for a business requirement
Plan a study laboratory using a trial tenant
Tell the difference between access management and identity governance

topics.title: Microsoft SC-400 Information Protection Administrator
topics.summary: Exam SC-400 was Microsoft's associate level certification for information protection and compliance administrators, and this page follows the objectives Microsoft published while the exam was live. Microsoft retired the exam in 2025 and moved that certification path to a newer exam, so treat this material as a study reference for the Microsoft Purview skills that carried over. The exam suited engineers who turn legal and regulatory requirements into technical controls for Microsoft 365 data. It

chapters.title: Implement data lifecycle and records management
Monitor and investigate data and activities with Microsoft Purview
Manage insider and privacy risk in Microsoft 365

objectives: Explain what the SC-400 exam measured and which role it served
Describe how Microsoft Purview classifies sensitive information
Choose a protection control for a given business requirement
Describe the current status of the exam and its replacement path

topics.title: Microsoft SC-900 Security, Compliance and Identity Fundamentals
topics.shortTitle: Microsoft SC-900 Security, Compliance and Identity Fundam...
topics.summary: Exam SC-900 is Microsoft's fundamentals level certification in security, compliance and identity, and it asks for no previous hands on experience. It suits business stakeholders, new IT staff and students who need to understand how Microsoft cloud security fits together. The exam is multiple choice and asks you to describe services rather than configure them, so it tests vocabulary and concepts instead of practical skill. Passing it earns the Microsoft Certified: Security, Compliance and Identit

chapters.title: Describe the concepts of security, compliance and identity
Describe the capabilities of Microsoft Entra
Describe the capabilities of Microsoft security solutions
Describe the capabilities of Microsoft compliance solutions

Define authentication, authorization and identity as a security boundary
Describe the main identity features of Microsoft Entra
Describe the Microsoft security services for cloud workloads and threat detection
Describe the Microsoft Purview compliance features for data protection

topics.title: OffSec OSCE
topics.summary: The Offensive Security Certified Expert, usually shortened to OSCE, was a practical, hands on certification from OffSec for penetration testers who could go beyond running existing tools. It sat at expert level, above OSCE's own entry exam, and it was widely treated as evidence that a candidate could find and exploit vulnerabilities by understanding how software actually breaks. Candidates had to complete a long, proctored lab under time pressure and then write a professional report explaining e
objectives: Explain how a program uses memory and how that knowledge leads to an exploitable flaw
Develop and debug working exploit code instead of relying on ready made tools
Identify and exploit weaknesses in network services and custom applications
Perform web application attacks that reach the underlying operating system
Move through a network from an initial foothold to further systems
Document each finding with evidence, impact and a practical fix

topics.title: OffSec OSCP
topics.summary: The OffSec Certified Professional (OSCP) is a fully hands-on penetration testing certification that requires candidates to compromise live, isolated target machines and an Active Directory set rather than answer multiple-choice questions. It is aimed at security practitioners who already hold solid networking, Linux and Windows administration fundamentals and who want to demonstrate that they can run an end-to-end assessment against realistic targets. For an employer, the credential is treated a

chapters.title: Vulnerability Scanning and Public Exploit Research

objectives: Information Gathering: enumerating hosts, services, shares and users to build an accurate picture of an unfamiliar target network before any exploitation is attempted.
Vulnerability Scanning and Public Exploit Research: validating automated scan output by hand, locating relevant public exploits and adapting them when they do not run unmodified.
Web Application Attacks: identifying and exploiting common server-side and client-side web flaws to obtain an initial foothold on a target host.
Client-Side Attacks: assessing user-facing delivery vectors such as document and browser-based lures, and recognising which endpoint controls reduce that risk.
Password Attacks: recovering or reusing credentials through offline cracking, online guessing and captured authentication material, and explaining the defensive controls that limit each route.
Windows Privilege Escalation: moving from a low-privileged shell to administrative rights by abusing misconfigurations, weak service permissions and exposed credentials.
Linux Privilege Escalation: escalating through SUID binaries, scheduled tasks, misconfigured services and leaked secrets on Linux hosts.
Port Redirection and Tunnelling: pivoting through a compromised host so that otherwise unreachable internal services can be assessed without breaking scope.
Active Directory Attacks: enumerating a domain, abusing authentication and delegation weaknesses, and chaining them toward domain-level objectives.
Post-Exploitation and Evidence Handling: stabilising access, collecting the artefacts that prove impact, and avoiding destructive actions on production-like targets.
Reporting and Professional Communication: producing a penetration test report with clear reproduction steps, evidence, business impact and prioritised remediation advice.

topics.title: OffSec OSED
topics.summary: OffSec OSED, the Exploit Developer certification from OffSec, is an advanced hands-on credential for security professionals who already write code and want to prove they can find and exploit memory corruption bugs in compiled Windows software. It sits at the expert end of the OffSec path, well above entry level. The exam is a practical, proctored challenge in which you are given a target application, must discover a vulnerability through fuzzing and reverse engineering, and then build a working

chapters.title: Penetration testing in a controlled environment
Exploit development for Windows user mode software
Exploit development for Windows kernel mode software
Penetration testing in an enterprise environment

objectives: Explain how Windows memory, the stack, and the heap support the execution of a compiled program
Read basic x86 assembly and link it back to the C source that produced it
Use a debugger to reproduce a crash and identify the exact instruction that fails
Fuzz a target application and triage the crashes it produces by severity
Describe the common exploit mitigations on Windows and how each one works
Build an exploit that redirects execution and runs your own payload on the target

topics.title: OffSec OSEP
topics.summary: OffSec OSEP, the Experienced Penetration Tester certification, is an advanced hands-on credential for penetration testers who already hold a working certification and now need to operate against defended, modern networks. It sits above entry level and assumes you can already run a basic engagement. The exam is a long practical assessment in which you attack a simulated enterprise while a security operations centre watches, so stealth and defence evasion matter as much as exploitation. OffSec doe

chapters.title: Penetration testing with a focus on operational security
Defence evasion and breaking out of restricted environments
Network and cloud security and pivoting
Microsoft Windows and Active Directory attacks

objectives: Write small custom tools in a scripting language to support an engagement
Evade antimalware and endpoint detection so your activity is not alerted on
Bypass application allow lists and other host controls on a Windows target
Move between network segments by using a compromised host as a pivot
Attack Active Directory environments and take control of the domain
Produce a professional assessment report that explains findings and business impact

topics.title: OffSec OSWA
topics.summary: The OffSec Web Assessor (OSWA) is an advanced, fully hands-on web application security certification built around OffSec's Advanced Web Attacks and Exploitation course, and it is aimed at experienced penetration testers, application security engineers and bug bounty hunters rather than newcomers. Candidates are expected to arrive already fluent in HTTP, browser security models and at least one server-side language, because the credential is designed to prove something narrower and deeper than ge

chapters.title: File Upload and Web Shell Risk

objectives: Web Assessment Methodology: scoping an application, mapping its attack surface and building a repeatable testing plan before attempting exploitation.
Source Code Review: reading server-side and client-side code to locate dangerous sinks, weak trust boundaries and logic flaws that black-box testing misses.
SQL Injection: identifying error-based, blind and second-order injection in custom application code, including reasoning about the filters intended to block it.
Cross-Site Scripting: finding stored, reflected and DOM-based execution contexts and explaining how output encoding and content security policy limit impact.
File Upload and Web Shell Risk: assessing upload functionality for type, extension and content filtering weaknesses and describing the post-exploitation risk they create.
OS Command and Argument Injection: tracing user input into process execution calls and evaluating the allow-lists and sanitisation intended to prevent it.
Server-Side Template Injection: recognising template engines that evaluate user input and assessing what functionality remains reachable when they do.
XML External Entity Injection: analysing XML parsers for external and parameter entity processing and the file and network reachability that follows.
Server-Side Request Forgery: testing URL and resource parameters for internal reachability, and treating network segmentation and metadata protections as the real boundary.
Insecure Deserialization: recognising serialized object formats in requests and cookies and assessing which gadget chains exist in the target technology stack.
Exploit Adaptation and Filter Bypass: adjusting known techniques for hardened, non-standard targets where off-the-shelf payloads fail to execute.
Reporting Web Findings: writing reproducible, evidence-backed findings with clear business impact and specific remediation guidance.

topics.title: OffSec OSWE
topics.summary: OffSec OSWE, the Web Expert certification, is an advanced hands-on credential for people who audit and attack web applications at source code level. It suits web developers moving into security, application security engineers, and penetration testers who want to go beyond black box testing. The exam is a practical, proctored challenge in which you receive applications with their source code, review that code to find vulnerabilities, and then exploit each finding to prove real impact. There is no

chapters.title: Source code analysis for web applications
Custom exploits for web applications and APIs

objectives: Read an unfamiliar web application code base and map its entry points
Identify the exact places where untrusted input reaches a dangerous operation
Recognise authentication and session handling flaws from source code alone
Assess injection and deserialisation weaknesses in server side code
Build a working exploit that proves the real world impact of each finding
Explain root cause and remediation to a development team in plain language

topics.title: Palo Alto PCNSA
topics.summary: Palo Alto Networks PCNSA, the Certified Network Security Administrator certification, is an entry level credential for engineers who operate next generation firewalls in daily production. It suits network security administrators, firewall operators, and support engineers in their first two years with the platform. The exam is delivered as multiple choice and scenario questions that test practical understanding of App ID, security policy, and NAT, and it is offered at test centres and online. Pas

chapters.title: Controlling traffic with App ID, content, and user identification

objectives: Describe how a next generation firewall controls traffic by application and user
Create and order security policies that allow only the traffic the business needs
Configure address translation so internal hosts can reach external networks
Use application and threat signatures to identify what is crossing the firewall
Read logs and session information to confirm whether a rule is working as intended
Follow safe administrative practice when managing a production firewall

topics.title: Palo Alto PCNSE
topics.summary: Palo Alto Networks PCNSE, the Certified Network Security Engineer certification, is the professional level credential for engineers who design, deploy, and troubleshoot the platform in complex environments. It suits experienced firewall engineers, network security architects, and consultants who already hold the administrator level certification or equivalent practice. The exam uses multiple choice and scenario based questions with detailed situations that require judgement rather than recall, a

chapters.title: Managing users and applying policy to them

objectives: Plan a firewall deployment that matches the size and risk of the environment
Configure core platform features such as interfaces, zones, routing, and high availability
Apply advanced security profiles, decryption, and denial of service protection
Design and manage address translation for complex inbound and outbound flows
Diagnose faults by using logs, session details, and packet captures
Explain the trade offs between deployment options to a customer or architect

topics.title: PortSwigger Burp Suite Certified Practitioner
topics.summary: The Burp Suite Certified Practitioner exam, code BSCP, is a four hour practical web security certification from PortSwigger, the company behind the Burp Suite testing tool. It is aimed at penetration testers, application security engineers and bug bounty hunters who already work through web vulnerability classes confidently and now want independent proof. The exam gives you two deliberately vulnerable applications, each solved in three stages: get into any user account, reach the admin interface

Chain two or more separate flaws together to reach a goal that neither flaw allows on its own
Escalate a foothold on the server side in order to read files or run commands
Deliver an attack that another user or an administrator will trigger in their own session
Work methodically against unlabelled targets and keep a clean record of the testing process

topics.title: Red Hat RHCSA
topics.summary: The Red Hat Certified System Administrator, usually called the RHCSA, is Red Hat's entry level certification for Linux administrators and carries the exam code EX200. It is aimed at engineers who already touch Red Hat Enterprise Linux in their daily work and want proof that they can configure, secure and repair a real server. Every task is performed on live systems, so an employer reads a pass as evidence of practical ability rather than memorized theory. The objectives are grouped into the ten
objectives: Explain what the RHCSA certification proves to a hiring manager
Describe how a performance based Linux exam is marked

Recognize which tasks must survive a system reboot

topics.title: Splunk Core Certified Power User
topics.summary: The Splunk Core Certified Power User credential, exam code SPLK-1002, is the second step in the Splunk certification path and sits above the entry level Core Certified User. It is aimed at analysts, engineers and security operations staff who already run basic searches and now need to build their own knowledge objects. Plan a study schedule based on the published section weights

topics.title: TCM Security PNPT
topics.summary: TCM Security PNPT, the Practical Network Penetration Tester certification, is a hands on credential for people who want to prove they can run a full penetration test from start to finish. It suits career changers entering offensive security, junior penetration testers, and students who learn best by doing guided labs. The exam is a five day practical assessment against a corporate network, followed by a report and a live debrief with an assessor, so writing and explaining your work counts as muc

chapters.title: Active Directory exploitation and privilege escalation

topics.title: Zero-Point Security CRTO
topics.summary: The Certified Red Team Operator (CRTO) from Zero-Point Security is a practical red team certification built around adversary simulation against a Windows Active Directory environment using Cobalt Strike and supporting tools. Active Directory is the Microsoft service that most companies use to manage users, computers and permissions, so it is the prize in most real intrusions. This certification sits at an advanced level and assumes you are already comfortable with Windows, command line work and

Evade common endpoint protections and report the operation clearly

The technique matters because a stolen domain credential gives an intruder legitimate access, so there is no malware to find and no exploit to patch, and the activity blends into ordinary administration. topics.shortTitle: Abuse of Information Repositories for Data Collection

It matters because these platforms concentrate design documents, credentials in notes and incident detail in one searchable place, and because the traffic is ordinary authenticated application use that endpoint tools cannot see. The telemetry that makes detec

topics.title: Abuse of PowerShell for Arbitrary Execution
topics.shortTitle: Abuse of PowerShell for Arbitrary Execution
topics.summary: This strategy detects abuse of PowerShell for arbitrary code execution on Windows, covering encoded commands, download and run patterns, and script hosts that launch PowerShell with unusual arguments. It matters because PowerShell is present on every modern Windows system, so an attacker needs no tooling on disk and can hide intent inside encoded arguments. Detection depends on process creation records with command line auditing, PowerShell script block and module logging, and network events tha

topics.summary: This strategy detects the removal or disabling of accounts and access rights as an impact action, using audit records from several platforms at once. The technique matters because an attacker who removes accounts or strips permissions can lock out responders and administrators, and the damage continues after the intrusion itself is contained. Detection depends on directory account change events, cloud identity audit records for user and role assignment changes, group membership events, and authe

topics.title: Account Manipulation Behavior Chain Detection
topics.summary: This strategy detects chains of account manipulation, where an actor creates an account, adds it to a privileged group or attaches credentials to an existing identity. The technique matters because account manipulation converts a single compromised session into durable, legitimate looking access that survives password resets and reboots. Detection works by correlating directory change events, group membership events and credential change events for the same target identity inside a short window.

topics.shortTitle: Application Exhaustion Flood Detection Across Platforms
topics.summary: This strategy covers application exhaustion flood, tracked as T1499.003, where an adversary drives an application to consume its finite resources so that real users cannot be served, without needing a large network flood. It matters because this is the denial of service variant that most often succeeds, since a single expensive search, report or upload endpoint can exhaust database connections, worker threads or memory from relatively few requests. topics.title: Automated Exfiltration Detection Strategy
topics.summary: This detection strategy targets automated exfiltration, where a tool rather than a person moves collected data out of the environment on a schedule or in repeated batches, matching the automated exfiltration technique. It matters because automation hides intent in volume: the individual transfer looks small, but the pattern across hours shows a steady drain toward one destination that the business does not use. topics.shortTitle: Automated File and API Collection Detection Across Platforms
topics.summary: This strategy detects automated collection, where an adversary uses scripting or built in command interpreters to gather files and data across a host or estate in bulk instead of browsing by hand. It matters because bulk collection converts a quiet foothold into a data theft pipeline, and because the collection commands often run through the same interpreters that administrators already use. Detection relies on process creation with full command lines, file access or read auditing on directories

topics.title: Detection of Upload Malware

The signal is statistical rather than exact: encoded argument flags, symbol density, string length and the difference between the written command and the command the interpreter finally runs.

topics.title: MoustachedBouncer
topics.summary: MoustachedBouncer is an espionage intrusion set that public reporting has tracked since around 2020 and links with moderate confidence to Belarus-aligned activity. topics.title: MuddyWater
topics.summary: MuddyWater is a widely tracked espionage activity set that public reporting has connected to Iranian state interests with moderate confidence, and vendors have labelled it Seedworm, Static Kitten and Mango Sandstorm among other names. topics.title: Mustang Panda
topics.summary: Mustang Panda is a China-nexus espionage cluster that public reporting describes as highly active and geographically broad, with sustained targeting of government, diplomatic, research, religious and non-governmental organisations across Asia, Europe and beyond. topics.title: Mustard Tempest
topics.summary: Mustard Tempest, tracked in public reporting as DEV-0206, TA569, GOLD PRELUDE, and UNC1543, is a financially motivated distribution operation rather than a classic intrusion team. topics.title: Naikon
topics.summary: Naikon is a cluster name for long-running espionage activity that public reporting associates with China-nexus operators and describes as concentrated on government, military, and civil organisations around the South China Sea and wider Southeast Asia. topics.title: NEODYMIUM
topics.summary: NEODYMIUM is a threat cluster described in public reporting as conducting targeted espionage against government, diplomatic, and political organisations, with strong regional emphasis on the Middle East. topics.title: Nomadic Octopus
topics.summary: Nomadic Octopus is a espionage cluster that public reporting associates with Central Asian interests and that has been tracked targeting government, diplomatic and telecommunications organisations, most notably in Afghanistan and neighbouring countries. topics.title: OilRig
topics.summary: OilRig, tracked by vendors as APT34, Helix Kitten, COBALT GYPSY and Hazel Sandstorm, is an espionage group whose activity public reporting associates with Iranian state interests. topics.title: Orangeworm
topics.summary: Orangeworm is a tracked activity set first described in public reporting around 2015 and best known for targeting the healthcare sector, including hospitals, clinics, insurance providers and the technology suppliers that serve them, with most reported victims in the United States and Europe and a smaller number in Asia. topics.title: Patchwork
topics.summary: Patchwork is an espionage cluster that public reporting tracks under several names, including Dropping Elephant, Operation Hangover and Monsoon. topics.title: PittyTiger
topics.summary: PittyTiger is an intrusion set that public reporting described in 2013 after a series of attacks against Indian government and military related organisations. The tradecraft was simple and cheap: spear phishing email with documents that exploited old, well known flaws in office and document reader software, followed by widely available remote access tools rather than custom malware. topics.title: PLATINUM
topics.summary: PLATINUM is the vendor label for a long-running espionage activity set that public reporting has tracked since about 2009 and generally assesses as state sponsored, though the sponsor is not openly confirmed. topics.title: POLONIUM
topics.summary: POLONIUM is a Lebanon linked espionage cluster that public reporting describes as focused on Israel and the wider Middle East, with targeting across critical infrastructure, healthcare, insurance, technology and government. topics.title: Poseidon Group
topics.summary: Poseidon Group is a financially motivated intrusion set that public reporting described as targeting businesses in several countries and sectors, including energy, manufacturing, finance, media, technology and services. topics.title: PROMETHIUM
topics.summary: PROMETHIUM is an espionage cluster best known from public reporting on the StrongPity toolset, which vendors have described in campaigns against users in Turkey, the Kurdish region, Italy, Belgium, and neighbouring areas. topics.title: Putter Panda
topics.summary: Putter Panda is an espionage cluster that public reporting linked to a unit of the Chinese military, with targets in satellite, aerospace, telecommunications and scientific research. topics.title: Rancor
topics.summary: Rancor is a modest but persistent espionage activity set that public reporting, notably from Palo Alto Networks around 2018, has linked to a suspected Southeast Asian state sponsor with low to moderate confidence. topics.title: Rocke

topics.title: Saint Bear
topics.summary: Saint Bear is a Russian-nexus intrusion set tracked under several vendor and national names, including Storm-0587 and UAC-0056, and public reporting describes sustained phishing campaigns against Ukrainian government bodies, military units, and their suppliers in Europe. topics.title: Salt Typhoon

topics.title: Sandworm Team
topics.summary: Sandworm Team, also tracked as Seashell Blizzard and APT44, is a Russian state-linked activity set that public reporting attributes to Russian military intelligence. topics.title: Sidewinder

topics.title: SilverTerrier

topics.title: Sowbug
topics.summary: Sowbug is an espionage cluster that public reporting has associated with activity against government and diplomatic targets in South America and Southeast Asia, with intrusion evidence described from around 2015 onward. topics.title: Star Blizzard
topics.summary: Star Blizzard is a Russian-nexus espionage cluster that public reporting, including statements from United Kingdom and United States authorities, links to a Russian intelligence service. topics.title: TeamTNT

topics.title: Thrip

topics.title: Tonto Team
topics.summary: Tonto Team is a China-nexus espionage cluster that public reporting describes as targeting government, military, diplomatic and technology organisations, mainly in Asia and Europe, with a long history of campaigns that blend credential phishing with exploitation of public-facing applications. topics.title: Transparent Tribe
topics.summary: Transparent Tribe is a espionage cluster that public reporting associates with South Asian state interests and that has focused for years on military, government and educational targets, mainly in India and neighbouring countries. topics.title: Tropic Trooper
topics.summary: Tropic Trooper, also reported as Pirate Panda and KeyBoy, is a long-running espionage cluster that public reporting describes targeting government, healthcare, research, retail and transport organisations in Taiwan and the Philippines, with activity tracked from around 2011 onward. topics.title: Turla
topics.summary: Turla is one of the longest-documented espionage intrusion sets, assessed by multiple governments and vendors as associated with Russian state security services, most commonly linked in public reporting to the Federal Security Service. topics.title: Velvet Ant

topics.title: Whitefly

topics.title: Active Directory Certificate Services
topics.summary: Active Directory Certificate Services, usually shortened to AD CS, is the Microsoft server role that turns a Windows domain into a public key infrastructure: it runs a certification authority, publishes certificate templates, and issues and revokes X.509 certificates for users, computers and services. topics.title: Adversarial Machine Learning
topics.summary: Adversarial machine learning is the study of how machine learning models can be manipulated through their inputs, their training data or their deployment environment. topics.title: Adversary Simulation
topics.summary: Adversary simulation is the practice of emulating a specific threat actor's known tactics, techniques and procedures against your own environment in order to test whether detection and response actually work. It is narrower and more deliberate than a penetration test, which normally optimises for finding and chaining exploitable vulnerabilities, and more targeted than automated breach and attack simulation, which replays a fixed technique library across many controls. topics.title: AES GCM
topics.summary: AES-GCM is an authenticated encryption with associated data (AEAD) mode that combines the AES block cipher in counter mode with a GHASH-based universal hash to produce ciphertext plus a 128-bit authentication tag, so confidentiality and integrity are delivered by a single key. The construction takes a 128-bit block cipher key (AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256), a unique nonce of typically 96 bits, the plaintext, and optional associated data that is authenticated but not encrypted. topics.title: AI Governance
topics.summary: AI governance is the set of policies, decision rights, controls and review processes an organisation uses to decide how artificial intelligence systems are proposed, approved, built, operated and retired. It spans the whole lifecycle rather than a single review: use case intake and risk classification, data sourcing and lawful basis, model evaluation and documentation, human oversight, monitoring for drift or harmful output, incident handling, and management of third party models and vendors. topics.title: AI Security
topics.summary: AI security covers two connected jobs: protecting artificial intelligence systems from attack, and using AI safely inside security operations. On the protection side it includes securing the model supply chain and weights, controlling who can read or change training data and prompts, constraining what an agent is permitted to do, sanitising untrusted content that reaches a model, and monitoring inputs and outputs for abuse. topics.title: Alert Fatigue
topics.summary: Alert fatigue is the degradation of analyst attention and judgement caused by a detection pipeline that raises more alerts than a team can meaningfully examine. It is not simply a volume problem. Fatigue sets in when alerts are numerous and individually low-yield, so that the rational response becomes pattern matching on the alert title, batch-closing whole categories, and treating the queue as work to be cleared rather than as evidence to be assessed. The operational consequences are measurable

topics.title: Alert Triage
topics.summary: Alert triage is the work of taking the queue of alerts a monitoring platform has produced and deciding, one by one, which of them deserve investigation, which can be closed, and which need to be escalated to someone else. It is deliberately not the same as detection engineering, which writes the rules, or incident response, which handles the confirmed incident. topics.title: Anti Forensics
topics.summary: Anti-forensics is the set of techniques an adversary uses to frustrate, mislead or delay forensic analysis, either by destroying evidence, by making analysis uneconomic, or by planting artefacts that send investigators down the wrong path. The category spans data destruction such as secure wiping, free-space overwriting and the deletion of logs; artefact manipulation including timestamp alteration, log tampering and the removal of entries from event or audit trails; concealment through encryptio

topics.title: Antimalware Scan Interface
topics.summary: The Antimalware Scan Interface is a Windows interface that lets applications and scripting runtimes hand content to the installed antimalware provider for inspection before that content is executed, interpreted or loaded. Its importance comes from the gap it fills: script engines and dynamic runtimes do not necessarily write a file to disk before running code, so a traditional file scanner sees nothing to inspect. By calling into AMSI, a participating host such as a scripting engine, an office m

topics.title: API Security
topics.summary: API security is the discipline of protecting application programming interfaces, the machine to machine interfaces that now carry most application traffic, including mobile clients, partner integrations and internal service calls. It focuses on authentication and per endpoint authorisation, per object authorisation, strict input and schema validation, rate limiting and quota, safe error handling, and the logging needed to reconstruct which principal called which resource. The structural differen

topics.title: Application Allowlisting
topics.summary: Application allowlisting, also called application control, is an endpoint control that permits only approved executables, scripts and libraries to run and blocks everything else by default. Enforcement happens in the kernel before a process is created, and each rule identifies a program by publisher signature, cryptographic hash, or path, usually with a fallback mode that records blocked attempts before it starts blocking them. topics.title: ARP
topics.summary: The Address Resolution Protocol, ARP, maps a known IPv4 address to a hardware address on the same local network segment. When a host needs to send a frame to an address such as 10[.]0[.]0[.]5 and has no cached entry, it broadcasts a request asking who holds that address, and the owner replies with its MAC address, which is then cached for a short period. The design has no authentication of replies, so any device on the segment can send an unsolicited response claiming an address it does not own.

topics.title: Attachment Sandboxing
topics.summary: Attachment sandboxing is an email security control that executes or opens a suspicious attachment in an isolated, instrumented environment before the message is delivered, then decides based on observed behaviour rather than on a signature. topics.title: Attack Surface Management
topics.summary: Attack surface management is the continuous process of discovering, inventorying, prioritising and reducing the set of ways an adversary can reach or influence an organisation. It has two halves that are often confused. External attack surface management discovers what is actually reachable from the internet, including forgotten subdomains, stale DNS records, exposed management interfaces, cloud storage and leaked credentials, and compares that reality with the official asset register. Internal

topics.title: Attribute-Based Access Control
topics.summary: Attribute-based access control (ABAC) is an access control model that evaluates a policy against attributes of the subject, the resource, the action and the environment at the moment of the request, rather than relying solely on a pre-assigned role. topics.title: Attribution
topics.summary: Attribution is the analytic judgement that links a set of observed activity to a responsible actor, and it is one of the most overclaimed products in cyber threat intelligence. Analysts distinguish at least three questions that are routinely conflated: technical attribution of tooling and infrastructure to a cluster of activity, operational attribution of that cluster to a consistent set of people and their tradecraft, and strategic or political attribution of those people to a state, sponsor or

topics.title: Audit Evidence
topics.summary: Audit evidence is the recorded information an auditor examines to test whether a control exists and operated as described throughout the period under review. Useful evidence must be relevant to the specific control, sufficient in quantity to support a conclusion, and reliable, which in practice means produced by the system rather than assembled by the person being assessed. Common types are configuration exports, system generated logs with trustworthy timestamps, tickets and approval records, ac

topics.title: Authenticated Scan
topics.summary: An authenticated scan, also called a credentialed scan, is a vulnerability assessment in which the scanner logs on to the target host with a dedicated account and inspects the system from the inside rather than inferring everything from network responses. With valid credentials the scanner can read the installed package inventory, patch level, kernel version, local configuration, registry or configuration files and service settings, so it reports installed but unpatched software accurately and p

topics.title: Bastion Host
topics.summary: A bastion host, also called a jump host or jump server, is a hardened and closely monitored system that acts as the single entry point for administrative access into a protected network segment. Administrators connect to the bastion first and reach internal systems from there, so the number of paths that accept management traffic collapses to one that can be restricted by source address, watched continuously and reviewed. topics.title: BGP Hijacking
topics.summary: The Border Gateway Protocol is the routing protocol that exchanges reachability information between autonomous systems on the internet, and it operates on trust: a network announces the address prefixes it can reach, and its neighbours generally believe the announcement. topics.title: Bootkit
topics.summary: A bootkit is malware that takes control of a system early in the boot process, before the operating system or its security software starts. It targets pre-operating-system code such as the master boot record on older systems, the bootloader, or UEFI firmware, and it may also install a malicious boot driver that loads at kernel start. Because it runs first, a bootkit can hide its own files and processes from the running system, weaken protections such as Secure Boot, and load further malware on e

topics.title: Bring Your Own Device
topics.summary: Bring your own device is the policy and technical model in which staff use personally owned phones, tablets, or laptops for work, with the organisation granting access to corporate data on hardware it does not own or fully control. topics.title: Broken Access Control
topics.summary: Broken access control is the class of application flaws where a system fails to enforce who is allowed to do what, so a user can reach data or actions beyond their intended permissions. topics.title: Bug Bounty Programme
topics.summary: A bug bounty programme is a formal arrangement in which an organisation invites independent security researchers to test defined systems and pays for valid, previously unknown vulnerabilities. It is governed first by scope, which names the domains, applications, and sometimes source repositories that may be tested, and by a set of rules covering prohibited techniques, data handling, and safe harbour language that protects good-faith research from legal action. Most programmes use a triage servic

topics.title: Business Continuity Plan
topics.summary: A business continuity plan is the documented set of arrangements that keeps an organisation's critical products and services available during and after a disruption, and returns them to normal in a controlled way. It is broader than disaster recovery: recovery planning concentrates on technology such as servers, data, and networks, while continuity also covers people, premises, suppliers, communications, and the manual workarounds that bridge the gap while systems are restored. The plan is built

topics.title: Business Email Compromise
topics.summary: Business email compromise is a fraud category in which an attacker abuses a trusted email identity, either by taking over a real mailbox or by impersonating one closely enough to be believed, and uses that trust to move money or data. Because the message comes from a genuine account or a convincing lookalike, it often passes ordinary spam and authentication checks, and the ask is usually a payment to a changed bank account, a change of payroll details, or the release of sensitive records. topics.title: Business Impact Analysis
topics.summary: A business impact analysis is the structured study that determines how the loss or degradation of each business process, and the resources that process depends on, would affect the organisation over time. topics.title: Business Impact Analysis
topics.summary: A business impact analysis is the analytical step that identifies an organisation's critical business processes, the resources they depend on, and the consequences of each process stopping for a given length of time. topics.title: C2 Beacon
topics.summary: A command-and-control beacon is the component of an intrusion that maintains a channel between implanted code on a victim host and infrastructure the operator controls, periodically checking in for instructions or waiting to be activated. topics.title: Case Management
topics.summary: Case management in a security operations centre is the discipline of grouping related alerts and evidence into a single investigation record that carries the work from first detection through triage, escalation, containment, closure, and lessons learned. topics.title: Certificate Authority
topics.summary: A certificate authority is the trusted entity that verifies the identity behind a public key and signs a certificate binding that identity to the key, which is what lets a client trust a server it has never met before. topics.title: Certificate Pinning
topics.summary: Certificate pinning is the practice of restricting which certificates or public keys a client will accept for a given service, instead of trusting every certificate authority in the platform trust store. The client embeds or is configured with an expected leaf certificate, a public key, a hash of either, or the identity of a specific issuing authority, and it rejects any chain that does not match. topics.title: Certificate Transparency
topics.summary: Certificate transparency is a public logging system for transport layer security certificates that requires certificate authorities to submit issued certificates to independent, append-only logs and to include proof of that submission in the certificate itself. topics.title: Chain OF Custody
topics.summary: Chain of custody is the documented, unbroken record of who collected a piece of evidence, when and where it was collected, how it was handled and stored, who accessed it afterwards, and how it was transferred between custodians. topics.title: CIS Benchmark
topics.summary: A CIS Benchmark is a configuration hardening baseline published by the Center for Internet Security for a specific technology and version, such as an operating system, a web server, a database, a cloud platform, or a container runtime. topics.title: CIS Critical Security Controls
topics.summary: The CIS Critical Security Controls are a prioritised set of defensive safeguards, published by the Center for Internet Security and maintained through a consensus process with input from government, industry, and practitioners. topics.title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities
topics.summary: The CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog is a public list, maintained by the United States Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, of vulnerabilities that have been observed being exploited in real incidents rather than merely being theoretically severe. topics.summary: Cloud audit logging records the control-plane activity of a cloud account: which identity called which API, from which address, at what time, with which parameters, and with what result. topics.title: Cloud IAM Policy
topics.summary: A cloud identity and access management policy is the machine-readable document that states which principal may perform which actions on which resources, and under what conditions, inside a cloud provider's control plane. topics.title: Cloud Incident Response
topics.summary: Cloud incident response is the set of prepared actions a team takes when a security event occurs in infrastructure a provider operates on the customer's behalf. The mechanics differ from on-premises work in three ways. topics.summary: Cloud key management is the practice of creating, storing, using, rotating and retiring cryptographic keys through a provider's managed service rather than inside application code. topics.title: Cloud Network Segmentation

topics.title: Cloud Security Posture Management
topics.summary: Cloud security posture management is the continuous, API-driven assessment of cloud configuration against an expected baseline. topics.title: Cloud Shared Responsibility Model
topics.summary: The shared responsibility model describes how security duties are divided between a cloud provider and its customer, and it is the mental model that most cloud security failures trace back to. topics.title: Cloud Workload Protection Platform
topics.summary: A cloud workload protection platform protects the running compute layer of a cloud estate, covering virtual machines, containers, serverless functions, and increasingly the orchestration control plane that schedules them. topics.title: Code Signing
topics.summary: Code signing is the use of a digital signature over a software artifact so that a consumer can verify who produced it and whether it has changed since it was signed. topics.title: Conditional Access
topics.summary: Conditional access is a policy engine that evaluates signals about a sign-in attempt and then decides whether to allow it, block it, or allow it only after additional requirements are satisfied such as multi-factor authentication, a compliant device or a trusted network location. topics.title: Confidence Level
topics.summary: Confidence is the explicit, calibrated expression of how much weight an analytic judgement should carry, and it is distinct from the likelihood that an event will occur. topics.title: Container Escape
topics.summary: Container escape is the class of techniques by which a process confined to a container reaches the underlying host, another tenant's container, or the cluster control plane, converting a workload compromise into infrastructure compromise. topics.title: Container Image Scanning
topics.summary: Container image scanning inspects the layers, package manifests and configuration of a container image to find known-vulnerable software components, embedded secrets, malware and risky settings before the image is deployed or while it sits in a registry. Scanners enumerate installed packages with their versions and match them against vulnerability data keyed by package name, version and distribution, and they also read image metadata such as the base image, exposed ports, user and build history.

topics.title: Container Registry Security

topics.title: Container Runtime Security

topics.title: Container Security

topics.title: Containment
topics.summary: Containment is the incident response phase in which a team deliberately limits the spread, impact and persistence of an active intrusion while preserving both the evidence and the business functions needed to recover. topics.title: Containment Strategy
topics.summary: Containment strategy is the deliberate plan for stopping the spread of an incident while preserving evidence, intelligence value and business function. It sits between detection and eradication in the incident response lifecycle, and is normally split into short-term containment, which buys time with the least disruptive action available, and long-term containment, which stabilises the environment until clean systems can be rebuilt. topics.title: Content Security Policy
topics.summary: Content Security Policy is a browser-enforced allowlist, delivered as a response header or a meta element, that restricts which sources a page may load scripts, styles, images, frames and connections from. topics.title: Control Gap
topics.summary: A control gap is the measurable difference between the protection an organisation believes it has and the protection that is actually implemented, operating and effective. Three distinct failure modes hide inside that single phrase, and separating them is the core skill. A design gap exists when no control addresses the risk at all, for example no privileged access review for a tier-zero identity store. topics.title: Control Testing
topics.summary: Control testing is the evidence-based evaluation of whether a stated control is designed to meet its objective and whether it actually operated throughout the period under review. topics.title: Cross-Border Data Transfer
topics.summary: Cross-border data transfer is any movement of personal data to a jurisdiction other than the one it was collected in, together with the legal and technical controls that make that movement lawful. topics.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery
topics.summary: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) is a web application flaw in which a victim's browser is tricked into sending an authenticated request that the user never intended to make. topics.title: Cross-Site Scripting

topics.title: Cryptographic Agility
topics.summary: Cryptographic agility is the property of a system that lets its algorithms, key sizes, protocol versions and certificate chains be replaced quickly without redesigning the application or recompiling firmware. topics.title: CVSS
topics.summary: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) is an open framework for describing the technical severity of a software vulnerability on a scale from zero to ten. It does not measure business risk on its own; it scores qualities such as how a flaw is reached, what access it requires, and what it affects. topics.title: Cyber Kill Chain
topics.summary: The Cyber Kill Chain is a seven-stage model of an intrusion that describes how an adversary progresses from reconnaissance to mission impact. The stages are reconnaissance, weaponisation, delivery, exploitation, installation, command and control, and actions on objectives. topics.title: Dark Web Monitoring
topics.summary: Dark web monitoring is the systematic collection and analysis of content from sources that mainstream search engines do not index, including criminal forums, illicit marketplaces, paste sites, private messaging channels, ransomware leak sites and credential dumps, in order to detect exposure, fraud enablers and threats to an organisation. topics.title: Data Classification
topics.summary: Data classification is the practice of assigning every information asset a label that states how sensitive it is, and therefore how it must be handled. topics.title: Data Loss Prevention
topics.summary: Data loss prevention (DLP) is the set of controls that watch data in motion, in use and at rest, and block or record it when it crosses a boundary the organisation has defined. Detection combines content inspection, such as matching patterns for card numbers or national identifiers, with context such as the sender, the destination and the volume, because content alone produces far too much noise. topics.title: Data Masking
topics.summary: Data masking replaces real sensitive values with realistic but false ones, so a copy of data can be used for testing, analytics or training without exposing the people in it. Static masking rewrites a copy in place, while dynamic masking changes values on the fly as a query returns them, leaving stored data untouched and usually driven by the requester's role. topics.title: Data Poisoning
topics.summary: Data poisoning is the deliberate corruption of the data used to train or fine-tune a machine learning model, so the finished model behaves badly on inputs the attacker chooses. The attacker may add mislabelled examples, flip existing labels, or inject a backdoor trigger that stays dormant until a rare pattern appears. topics.title: Data Protection Impact Assessment
topics.summary: A Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) is a structured review carried out before processing that is likely to result in a high risk to people's rights and freedoms. It describes the processing, records why it is necessary and proportionate, sets out the risks to individuals, and lists the measures that reduce those risks. topics.title: Data Retention
topics.summary: Data retention is the practice of deciding in advance how long each category of data is kept and what happens when that period ends. A retention schedule names the data, the lawful or business reason for holding it, the period, the storage location and the destruction method, because keeping data indefinitely increases both breach impact and legal exposure once it can no longer be justified. Periods are usually set by whichever is longer, a legal or contractual duty or a genuine operational need

topics.title: Data Subject Access Request
topics.summary: A data subject access request (DSAR) is a request from an individual asking an organisation to confirm whether it holds personal data about them and to provide a copy, together with related rights such as correction, deletion or objection. topics.title: Deception Technology
topics.summary: Deception technology places believable but fake assets on a network, such as decoy servers, file shares, credentials and documents, so an intruder who is already inside reveals themselves by touching something no legitimate user has a reason to touch. Alerts from these lures are high fidelity because the decoys carry no production traffic, which lets defenders skip a long triage queue and act on a signal that is almost always malicious. topics.title: Defence in Depth
topics.summary: Defence in depth is the principle of layering independent security controls so that the failure of any single control does not lead directly to compromise. It comes from military thinking about overlapping defensive positions, and it appears in security architecture as identity checks, network segmentation, hardened hosts, endpoint detection, monitoring and recovery arranged so an attacker must defeat several different mechanisms. topics.title: Demilitarised Zone
topics.summary: A demilitarised zone, or DMZ, is a network segment that sits between an untrusted network such as the internet and the protected internal network, and it hosts services that outside users must reach. topics.title: Detection as Code
topics.summary: Detection as code is the practice of managing detection content, meaning rules, correlation logic, enrichment mappings and the tests that validate them, with the same engineering discipline applied to application source code. Detection logic lives in a version control repository rather than being clicked into a console. Changes arrive as reviewed pull requests with an author, a reviewer and a written rationale. Every rule carries structured metadata: an identifier, a description, the ATT&CK tech

topics.title: Detection Use Case Management
topics.summary: Detection use case management is the discipline of running detection content as a managed product rather than a collection of ad hoc rules. It covers the lifecycle of a use case: deriving a detection requirement from threat intelligence, incident lessons or control gaps, documenting the behaviour and the data sources it needs, writing and testing the logic against sample or replayed data, deploying it with an owner and a response procedure, then measuring its health through alert volume, false p

topics.title: DevSecOps
topics.summary: DevSecOps is the practice of building security work into the software delivery pipeline so that checks run continuously and automatically rather than in a review gate at the end. It redistributes responsibility: developers fix findings in the tools they already use, platform teams expose secure defaults and reusable components, and security engineers build the tests, policies and paved roads. topics.title: DHCP
topics.summary: The Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) lets a client that has no address ask a local server for one, and receive an address, a subnet mask, a default gateway, name server addresses and other options for a fixed lease period. The exchange is a four step conversation, usually described as discover, offer, request and acknowledge, and it runs over the local link using broadcast before the client has any routable address at all. topics.title: Diamond Model
topics.summary: The Diamond Model is an intrusion analysis framework that describes every malicious event as the interaction of four core features: an adversary, a capability, an infrastructure and a victim. The adversary is the actor or group directing activity. The capability is the tool, malware, exploit or credential the actor wields. topics.title: Disaster Recovery Testing
topics.summary: Disaster recovery testing is the planned exercise of restoring systems and data from backups and alternative arrangements in order to prove that recovery targets can actually be met. A test is designed around measurable objectives, usually a recovery time objective for how long an outage may last and a recovery point objective for how much data may be lost, and it must produce evidence: how long the restore took, what failed, and which runbook step was wrong. topics.title: Disk Forensics
topics.summary: Disk forensics is the practice of acquiring and analysing the contents of storage media, such as hard drives, solid state drives, USB keys and virtual disks, to reconstruct what happened on a system. The discipline rests on two principles: acquire before you analyse, and work from a write-blocked copy rather than the original. topics.title: Disk Imaging
topics.summary: Disk imaging is the process of creating a bit-for-bit copy of a storage device, or of a defined set of allocated and unallocated regions, so that examination happens on a working copy while the original remains sealed and unmodified. topics.title: Distributed Denial of Service
topics.summary: A distributed denial of service attack attempts to make a service unavailable by exhausting a resource, using many sources so that no single host can simply be blocked. Volume-based attacks saturate network links with floods of packets or bytes. Protocol attacks consume state on network devices or servers, for example by exhausting connection tables or abusing a handshake so that half-open sessions accumulate. topics.title: DKIM
topics.summary: DomainKeys Identified Mail, usually shortened to DKIM, is an email authentication method that lets a sending domain attach a cryptographic signature to a message so a receiving system can verify that the message really came from that domain and was not altered on the way. topics.title: DMARC
topics.summary: DMARC, short for Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance, is a published policy that tells receiving mail systems what to do when a message claiming to be from your domain fails authentication. topics.title: DNS Security
topics.summary: DNS security covers the protection of the domain name system itself and the defensive use of DNS data. The domain name system is a globally distributed, largely unauthenticated directory that turns names into addresses, so it is both an attractive target and a rich source of evidence. topics.summary: DNS tunnelling is a technique for carrying arbitrary data inside DNS queries and responses, exploiting the fact that name resolution is permitted almost everywhere, including networks where most other outbound traffic is blocked. topics.title: DNSSEC
topics.summary: DNSSEC, the Domain Name System Security Extensions, adds cryptographic signatures to DNS answers so a resolver can verify that a record came from the zone that owns it and arrived unmodified. topics.title: Dynamic Application Security Testing
topics.summary: Dynamic application security testing is the automated assessment of a running application, sending crafted requests or driving a browser and analysing the responses for security weaknesses such as injection, broken authentication, insecure session handling, misconfigured headers, exposed administrative interfaces and unsafe redirects. topics.title: ECDSA
topics.summary: ECDSA is the elliptic curve analogue of the Digital Signature Algorithm, producing signatures whose security depends on the hardness of the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem rather than integer factorisation. topics.title: EDR
topics.summary: Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) is a class of endpoint agent that continuously records process, file, registry, network and identity telemetry from a host, applies behavioural analytics and signature logic to that stream, and gives responders the ability to query, isolate and remediate the endpoint remotely. topics.title: Endpoint Detection and Response
topics.summary: Endpoint detection and response, or EDR, is a class of tooling that continuously records activity on hosts such as laptops, servers and virtual machines, then gives analysts the ability to investigate and act on what it recorded. topics.title: EPSS
topics.summary: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System, or EPSS, is a data-driven model that estimates the probability a published software vulnerability will be exploited in the wild within the next thirty days. topics.title: Eradication
topics.summary: Eradication is the incident response phase in which the team removes the adversary's ability to continue operating in the environment: malware, tooling, persistence mechanisms, created or compromised accounts, malicious configuration, and the initial access vector that let them in. topics.title: Evasion
topics.summary: Evasion is the set of techniques used to avoid, delay or defeat detection and analysis rather than to achieve an objective directly, and it is best understood as a tax on defenders' visibility rather than a single action. Practitioners group it by what is being evaded: signature matching, behavioural analytics, logging, and human investigation. topics.title: Exfiltration
topics.summary: Exfiltration is the unauthorised transfer of data from an environment the organisation controls to a destination it does not, and it is usually the point at which an intrusion becomes a reportable breach. topics.title: Exploit Development
topics.summary: Exploit development is the offensive engineering discipline of turning a software vulnerability into a reliable, repeatable demonstration that the weakness can be triggered and its consequences controlled. topics.title: Exploit Maturity
topics.summary: Exploit maturity describes how far exploitation of a particular vulnerability has progressed in the real world, from a theoretical description through a proof of concept that works only in ideal conditions, to a functional and reliable exploit, to weaponised code embedded in widely used attack tooling or automated mass scanners. topics.title: Extended Detection and Response
topics.summary: Extended detection and response, or XDR, is an architectural approach that collects telemetry from several security control points, such as endpoint agents, network sensors, mail gateways, identity providers and cloud workloads, into one place where it is correlated, searched and acted on. topics.title: FAIR Risk Model
topics.summary: The FAIR risk model, where FAIR stands for Factor Analysis of Information Risk, is an approach to expressing cyber and operational risk in measurable terms instead of qualitative labels. topics.title: False Positive Triage
topics.summary: False positive triage is the review process that separates findings describing a real problem from findings describing the normal, expected behaviour of a system. In vulnerability management the same term covers scanner output that cannot be exploited in the deployed configuration, such as a library version flagged by a signature match when the vulnerable code path is never loaded or is unreachable from the network. topics.title: FedRAMP
topics.summary: FedRAMP, the Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program, is a United States government programme that standardises how cloud services are assessed, authorised and continuously monitored before agencies may use them. topics.title: Fileless Malware
topics.summary: Fileless malware is malicious logic that executes without a conventional malicious file ever being written to disk in a form that a scanner can inspect, instead living in memory, in registry values, in system configuration stores, or in the command lines and scripts passed to legitimate interpreters already present on the host. topics.title: Firewall
topics.summary: A firewall is a network security control that enforces an explicit policy over which traffic may pass between two zones by inspecting packet headers and, in modern products, application-layer content. topics.title: Flash Report
topics.summary: A flash report is a short, time-sensitive threat intelligence product published quickly to warn recipients about an urgent development and prompt a defensive decision. It is deliberately narrow: one topic, minimal background, and heavy emphasis on what changed, why it matters now, what recipients should do, and when the next update is expected.
